entries.name: vars (string values)
entries.cloudflare: Each string in vars appears on env as a string.
entries.orange: Wrangler converts each string var to a plain_text binding, and Orange puts the string on env.
entries.notes: Named environments follow Wrangler's rules, because Orange reads the config with Wrangler's unstable_readConfig.

entries.name: vars (JSON values)
entries.cloudflare: Each non-string value in vars appears on env as a parsed JSON value.
entries.orange: Wrangler converts each non-string var to a json binding, and Orange puts the value on env.
entries.notes: A .dev.vars or .env key with the same name replaces the JSON value with a string.

entries.name: .dev.vars secrets
entries.cloudflare: wrangler dev loads keys from .dev.vars (or .dev.vars.<env>) into env as secret text.
entries.orange: Orange calls Wrangler's unstable_getVarsForDev, so .dev.vars keys reach env as strings, like wrangler dev.
entries.notes: A .dev.vars key replaces a var with the same name. It does not replace a binding of another type, such as a Secrets Store secret. When the config has secrets.required, only listed keys and keys that are also vars load, and a missing required key prints a warning.

entries.name: .env secrets
entries.cloudflare: When no .dev.vars file exists, wrangler dev loads .env files into env as secret text.
entries.orange: Orange gets the same behavior from Wrangler's unstable_getVarsForDev. A .env key reaches env as a string.
entries.notes: Orange passes no custom env file list, so Wrangler reads its default .env files. CLOUDFLARE_LOAD_DEV_VARS_FROM_DOT_ENV and CLOUDFLARE_INCLUDE_PROCESS_ENV apply as in Wrangler. Verified by loading a config with a .env file and no .dev.vars.
entries.unverified: Not covered by a repository test. Verified once by a manual config load on the devbox.

entries.name: secrets_store_secrets
entries.cloudflare: get() returns the secret value from the account Secrets Store.
entries.orange: get() reads the value from .dev.vars in the project root, then from the host process.env.
entries.notes: Orange does not call the Secrets Store API and does not read .env files for this binding. A missing value rejects with Secrets Store binding "<NAME>" is not configured locally.

entries.name: version_metadata
entries.cloudflare: env binding with the Worker version id (a UUID), the version tag, and the version timestamp.
entries.orange: id is a SHA-256 hex digest of the bundle and the normalized config. tag is always "dev". timestamp is the build time.
entries.notes: The id changes only when code or config changes. Code that parses id as a UUID fails.

entries.name: unsafe.bindings unsafe_eval
entries.cloudflare: The unsafe_eval binding has eval(), newFunction(), newAsyncFunction(), and newWasmModule().
entries.orange: Wrangler emits unsafe_unsafe_eval, and Orange maps it to an UnsafeEval object built on node:vm.
entries.notes: unsafe-test passes 4 of 5. basics fails because a plain eval('') does not throw in Orange. Workerd forbids code generation outside the binding.

entries.name: unsafe.bindings of a type other than unsafe_eval
entries.cloudflare: Passes a binding of any type through to the Workers runtime without Wrangler validation.
entries.orange: Wrangler emits unsafe_<type>. Orange loads it as a stub that throws unsafe_<type> binding "<NAME>" is not supported by OpenOrange. See the OpenOrange bindings documentation for supported bindings.
entries.notes: Config load prints a [config-warning] line. Any member read returns a function that throws the message synchronously when called. Code that never calls the binding keeps working. The unsafe key is accepted only when it holds bindings and nothing else.

entries.name: kv_namespaces (Workers KV)
entries.cloudflare: Binds a Workers KV namespace: a global, eventually consistent key-value store with edge caching.
entries.orange: Each namespace id is an Orange-internal SQLite Durable Object on Rivet Actors. Data persists under .open-orange/rivetkit across orange dev restarts.
entries.notes: Reads see writes at once. Cloudflare can take 60 seconds or more to show a write in other locations. Orange has no edge cache. The local id is preview_id, then id, then the binding name, like wrangler dev. Upstream kv-test fails 0 of 5 because the conformance runner drops workerd kvNamespace bindings, not because of Orange's KV.

entries.name: KV get()
entries.cloudflare: get(key) returns the value as text, or null when the key is absent.
entries.orange: Same result. Key validation and error text follow workerd and Miniflare.
entries.notes: cacheTtl is validated (at least 30) and then ignored, because Orange has no cache. Expired keys read as null.

entries.name: KV get() with a type
entries.cloudflare: get(key, type) returns text, json, arrayBuffer, or stream values.
entries.orange: Supports the same four types and rejects other types with workerd's error text.
entries.notes: A stream value is the whole value buffered in one chunk.

entries.name: KV getWithMetadata()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the value, its metadata, and cacheStatus.
entries.orange: Returns value, metadata, and cacheStatus.
entries.notes: cacheStatus is always null, because Orange has no cache.

entries.name: KV get() with an array of keys
entries.cloudflare: Returns a Map for up to 100 keys. Only text and json types are allowed.
entries.orange: Same Map result, type rules, no Cloudflare key-count or size limit.
entries.notes: getWithMetadata() with an array returns value and metadata per key.

entries.name: KV put() with expiration and metadata
entries.cloudflare: Writes a string, ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferView, or stream with optional expiration, expirationTtl, and metadata.
entries.orange: Accepts the same value types and options, without Cloudflare's key, value, metadata, or TTL limits. A put of 128 MiB or more fails with Rivet's commit limit.
entries.notes: A stream value is read fully into memory before the write. Expired keys are removed when they are next read.

entries.name: KV delete()
entries.cloudflare: Deletes one key. Deleting an absent key succeeds.
entries.orange: Deletes the row from the namespace's SQLite table. An absent key succeeds.
entries.notes: Key validation matches get() and put().
entries.unverified: No repository test calls delete(). Verified by reading the code only.

entries.name: KV list() with prefix, limit, and cursor
entries.cloudflare: Lists keys in byte order with an opaque cursor, up to 1000 keys per page.
entries.orange: Lists keys in UTF-8 byte order with prefix, limit, and cursor. Expired keys are left out.
entries.notes: The cursor is the base64url form of the last key. Code must treat it as opaque, as on Cloudflare.

entries.name: KV deleteBulk()
entries.cloudflare: Not deployed. Workerd adds deleteBulk() only with the experimental flag, for tests.
entries.orange: KVNamespace has no deleteBulk() method.
entries.notes: kv-test deleteBulkTest fails because the runner drops the KV binding.

entries.name: d1_databases (D1)
entries.cloudflare: Binds a D1 database: managed SQLite with optional read replicas.
entries.orange: Each database id is an Orange-internal SQLite Durable Object on Rivet Actors. Data persists under .open-orange/rivetkit across orange dev restarts.
entries.notes: Every query goes to one local primary, so there are no read replicas. The local id is preview_database_id, then database_id, then the binding name. The D1 client follows workerd's HTTP-based client, and the backend follows Miniflare's D1 backend. orange d1 migrations apply/list and orange d1 execute write the same local store that orange dev reads.

entries.name: D1 prepare()
entries.cloudflare: Makes a prepared statement from SQL.
entries.orange: Makes a statement that runs on the D1 Rivet Actor.
entries.notes: Byte arrays are stored as BLOBs and read back as arrays of numbers.

entries.name: D1 bind()
entries.cloudflare: Binds numbers, strings, booleans, null, and byte arrays.
entries.orange: Same conversions as workerd: booleans become 1 or 0, and ArrayBuffers become byte arrays. Other types fail with D1_TYPE_ERROR.
entries.notes: Byte arrays are stored as BLOBs and read back as arrays of numbers.

entries.name: D1 first()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the first row, one column of it, or null.
entries.orange: Same result. A missing column fails with D1_COLUMN_NOTFOUND: Column not found (<name>).
entries.notes: Matches workerd's client code.

entries.name: D1 all()
entries.cloudflare: Returns results and meta for a statement.
entries.orange: Returns results and meta with changes, last_row_id, rows_read, rows_written, size_after, and duration.
entries.notes: meta.served_by is "open-orange.db", and served_by_primary is always true.

entries.name: D1 raw()
entries.cloudflare: Returns rows as arrays, with an optional first row of column names.
entries.orange: Same result, including the columnNames option.
entries.notes: Matches workerd's client code.

entries.name: D1 run()
entries.cloudflare: Runs a statement and returns meta.
entries.orange: Runs the statement through the /execute path and returns the backend result.
entries.notes: Like Miniflare, the result also has results.

entries.name: D1 batch()
entries.cloudflare: Runs statements in one transaction. A failure rolls back the whole batch.
entries.orange: Runs the statements in one storage transaction. A failure rolls back the batch.
entries.notes: Overlapping requests keep every insert.

entries.name: D1 exec()
entries.cloudflare: Runs raw SQL, one statement per line, and returns count and duration.
entries.orange: Splits the input by line like workerd and reports the failing line in D1_EXEC_ERROR.
entries.notes: Empty input fails with No SQL statements detected.

entries.name: D1 dump()
entries.cloudflare: Deprecated. Returns the database file for databases from the D1 alpha.
entries.orange: The backend has no dump route, so dump() always rejects with D1_DUMP_ERROR: Status + 404.
entries.notes: The error does not say that Orange does not support dump().
entries.unverified: Not run. Follows from the backend routing only /query and /execute.

entries.name: D1 withSession()
entries.cloudflare: Sessions give sequential consistency across read replicas.
entries.orange: Sessions work. Every query reaches the one primary, so reads are always current.
entries.notes: Bookmarks are local strings made from a timestamp and a counter. A bookmark from Cloudflare has no meaning in Orange.

entries.name: D1 session getBookmark()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the latest bookmark of the session.
entries.orange: Returns a local bookmark made from a timestamp and a counter.
entries.notes: Bookmarks are local strings made from a timestamp and a counter. A bookmark from Cloudflare has no meaning in Orange.

entries.name: durable_objects (class in this Worker)
entries.cloudflare: Binds a Durable Object class from this Worker. The class can use the SQLite or the KV storage backend.
entries.orange: Binds the class when a new_sqlite_classes migration creates it. The namespace runs on Rivet Actors.
entries.notes: Classes from new_classes (KV backend) fail config load with Unsupported Durable Object migration fields. See the Durable Object entries for API details.

entries.name: durable_objects (class in another Worker)
entries.cloudflare: Binds a Durable Object class that another Worker exports, with script_name.
entries.orange: The class runs in the Worker named by script_name, in the same orange dev session and on the same Rivet Engine. Stubs from both Workers reach one object.
entries.notes: A script_name outside the session gives a namespace whose stubs answer fetch() with 503 and throw on RPC, like Wrangler's dev registry. A binding with only environment or namespace_id still loads a stub.

entries.name: services (this Worker's default entrypoint)
entries.cloudflare: A service binding can target the Worker itself.
entries.orange: A binding whose service equals the config name calls the default export in process.
entries.notes: The config must set name. Without name, Orange treats every service binding as a binding to another Worker and loads a stub.

entries.name: services with entrypoint (named entrypoint in this Worker)
entries.cloudflare: entrypoint selects a named WorkerEntrypoint export of the target Worker.
entries.orange: Calls the named export of this Worker. A missing export fails with Worker has no entrypoint named "<name>".
entries.notes: The repository end-to-end test passes. Upstream namedServiceBinding hangs for 60 seconds in all four js-rpc test files.
entries.unverified: The cause of the namedServiceBinding hang is not found.

entries.name: services with props
entries.cloudflare: props on a service binding appear as ctx.props in the target entrypoint.
entries.orange: Config props and ctx.exports.<Name>({ props }) reach ctx.props. Overlapping calls see only their own props.
entries.notes: ctx-props-test fails only its ctx-props-test-disabled case, which tests a Worker without the props flag.

entries.name: Service binding fetch()
entries.cloudflare: fetch() on a service binding sends an HTTP request to the target's fetch handler.
entries.orange: Calls the entrypoint's fetch() in process. It follows redirects like workerd's fetch() and passes caller aborts to the callee.
entries.notes: In a Durable Object, the request waits until earlier writes are durable.

entries.name: Service binding JS RPC
entries.cloudflare: Methods and properties of a WorkerEntrypoint are callable over JS RPC.
entries.orange: Each call gets a new entrypoint instance in process. js-rpc-test passes 28 of 33.
entries.notes: Fails: disposal (not implemented), namedServiceBinding and portAbortCall (hang), sendStubOverRpc, and serializeHttpTypes. See the runtime API entries for RPC details.

entries.name: Service binding connect()
entries.cloudflare: connect() opens a socket to the target Worker's connect handler.
entries.orange: Opens an in-process socket to the entrypoint's connect() handler of this Worker. In a Durable Object, the connection opens after earlier writes are durable. The handler's end closes when its promise settles.
entries.notes: A target without connect() fails with Handler does not export a connect() function. A binding to another Worker is a stub (see Service binding to another Worker). js-rpc-test connectBinding passes. connect-handler-test localAddressViaServiceBinding fails only because the conformance runner drops its binding.

entries.name: services (another Worker)
entries.cloudflare: Calls a different Worker over fetch, JS RPC, or connect().
entries.orange: orange dev -c a -c b runs both Workers. fetch() and JS RPC reach the other Worker's default or named entrypoint over loopback HTTP. A Worker outside the session answers 503 on fetch() and throws on RPC with Wrangler's dev registry message.
entries.notes: connect() and WebSocket upgrades to another Worker throw. Workers in separate orange dev processes do not find each other.
entries.workaround: Pass every Worker to one orange dev with repeated -c.

entries.name: ctx.exports loopback bindings
entries.cloudflare: ctx.exports exposes this Worker's entrypoints as service stubs and its Durable Object classes as namespaces.
entries.orange: Builds ctx.exports from the Worker's named exports: entrypoints become loopback service stubs, and Durable Object classes become namespaces, including classes without a binding.
entries.notes: ctx.exports in a Durable Object throws DurableObjectState.exports is not implemented. import { exports } from "cloudflare:workers" reads the same object.

entries.name: import { env } from "cloudflare:workers"
entries.cloudflare: The env object is importable at module scope and in handlers.
entries.orange: The importable env is the same object as the handler env, readable while the module evaluates.
entries.notes: importable-env-test fails because the runner drops its KV binding. disable-importable-env-test fails because Orange ignores the disallow_importable_env flag.

entries.cloudflare: assets.binding gives the Worker a Fetcher for its static assets.
entries.orange: env.ASSETS.fetch() serves the assets directory with not_found_handling and follows redirects like a Fetcher.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: send_email
entries.cloudflare: Sends email from the Worker through Email Routing.
entries.orange: With ORANGE_EMAIL_SMTP_URL set to an smtp:// or smtps:// URL, send() delivers through that SMTP server. It takes an EmailMessage with its own MIME, or a message object with from, to, cc, bcc, replyTo, subject, text, html, headers, and attachments, and returns { messageId }. destination_address, allowed_destination_addresses, and allowed_sender_addresses are checked before anything is sent.
entries.notes: Without ORANGE_EMAIL_SMTP_URL, the binding is a stub whose calls throw Send Email binding "<NAME>" is not supported by OpenOrange. Set ORANGE_EMAIL_SMTP_URL to your SMTP server, or send email through your provider's HTTP API with fetch(). When the server fails, send() throws an error that names the server without its credentials. Orange does not check sender domains or verified destinations. Incoming email handlers are a handler entry. See docs/modules/email.mdx.

entries.name: browser
entries.cloudflare: Gives the Worker a headless browser through Browser Rendering.
entries.orange: With ORANGE_BROWSER_CDP_URL set to a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint (ws://, wss://, or an http:// address whose /json/version names one), the binding answers the requests of @cloudflare/puppeteer 1.x: launch(), the DevTools WebSocket of a session, sessions(), history(), and limits().
entries.notes: Without ORANGE_BROWSER_CDP_URL, the binding is a stub whose calls throw Browser Rendering binding "<NAME>" is not supported by OpenOrange. Set ORANGE_BROWSER_CDP_URL to a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint. Sessions on one self-run browser share it and its cookies, and browser.close() closes only the session's pages. keep_alive, location, and recording are ignored, and session limits are not enforced. See docs/modules/browser-rendering.mdx.

entries.name: workflows (workflow)
entries.cloudflare: Creates and controls Workflow instances that run durable steps, sleeps, and event waits.
entries.orange: Each instance is a Durable Object of the Orange-internal class openorange:workflow-engine on a Rivet Actor, running Cloudflare's Workflows engine from workers-sdk (workflows-shared at 4a5377fc), the engine of wrangler dev. create(), createBatch(), get(), deleteBatch(), and status(), pause(), resume(), terminate(), restart() (also from a step), delete(), and sendEvent() work. Steps awaited together run concurrently. The earliest timer is the object's alarm, so instances continue after their actor sleeps and across orange dev restarts.
entries.notes: Step output is bounded by Rivet's 128 MiB commit, not Cloudflare's 1 MiB. A duplicate ID is rejected, also for concurrent creates. Errors keep their names, as workerd's RPC keeps them from compatibility date 2026-04-21; wrangler dev's engine runs on 2024-10-22 and renames them. The status waiting is reported whenever the run only waits. limits.steps and subscribe() are not implemented. terminate() cannot stop a step callback that is already running. A binding with another Worker's script_name runs the Workflow in that Worker of the orange dev session. See docs/modules/workflows.mdx.

entries.name: queues.producers (queue)
entries.cloudflare: Sends messages to a Cloudflare Queue.
entries.orange: Each queue is an Orange-internal Rivet Actor whose RivetKit queue stores the messages. send() and sendBatch() with the text, bytes, json, and v8 content types, delaySeconds, delivery_delay, and metrics() work, and messages persist across orange dev restarts.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's message and batch limits are not copied. One send() or sendBatch() is one message to the Rivet Engine, at most 32 MiB. The registry raises maxIncomingMessageSize to 32 MiB so that one sendBatch() fits in one action request. Upstream queue-test fails because the conformance runner drops its queue binding. See docs/modules/queues.mdx.

entries.name: r2_buckets (r2_bucket)
entries.cloudflare: Reads and writes objects in an R2 bucket.
entries.orange: Each bucket_name is an Orange-internal SQLite Durable Object on Rivet Actors that stores bodies in 512 KiB chunks. head(), get(), put(), delete(), list(), conditional and range requests, checksums, and multipart uploads work, and objects persist across orange dev restarts. A bucket can use an S3-compatible store instead through ORANGE_R2_<BUCKET>_S3_* variables.
entries.notes: On the default backend, one Rivet Actor stores each bucket, so Rivet's storage limit for one actor bounds the bucket. ssecKey throws NotSupportedError. Puts accept streams of any length. The S3 backend restores custom metadata key case from an orange-r2-key-case metadata entry. Upstream r2-test fails because the conformance runner drops workerd's r2Bucket binding. See docs/modules/r2.mdx.

entries.cloudflare: Loads and runs dynamic Workers from code at runtime.
entries.orange: Each dynamic Worker runs in its own Node.js process. get() caches by name, load() and get(null) start fresh Workers. fetch(), RPC, env and props capabilities, globalOutbound null or Fetcher, and js/cjs/text/data/json/wasm modules work.
entries.notes: getDurableObjectClass(), entrypoint connect(), Python modules, and compiled WebAssembly.Module values throw. Compatibility settings, limits, and tails are ignored. See docs/modules/worker-loader.mdx.

entries.name: vpc_services (vpc_service)
entries.cloudflare: Reaches a private service through Workers VPC.
entries.orange: Loads a stub that throws VPC service binding "<NAME>" is not supported by OpenOrange. See the OpenOrange bindings documentation for supported bindings.
entries.notes: Config load prints a [config-warning] line. Any member read returns a function that throws the message synchronously when called. Code that never calls the binding keeps working.

entries.name: vpc_networks (vpc_network)
entries.cloudflare: Reaches a private network through Workers VPC.
entries.orange: Loads a stub that throws VPC network binding "<NAME>" is not supported by OpenOrange. See the OpenOrange bindings documentation for supported bindings.
entries.notes: Config load prints a [config-warning] line. Any member read returns a function that throws the message synchronously when called. Code that never calls the binding keeps working.

entries.name: unsafe_hello_world
entries.cloudflare: An example binding in Wrangler's schema. Wrangler marks it as do not use.
entries.orange: Loads a stub that throws unsafe_hello_world binding "<NAME>" is not supported by OpenOrange. See the OpenOrange bindings documentation for supported bindings.
entries.notes: Config load prints a [config-warning] line. Any member read returns a function that throws the message synchronously when called. Code that never calls the binding keeps working.

entries.name: fetch handler (object default export)
entries.cloudflare: export default { fetch(request, env, ctx) } handles each HTTP request.
entries.orange: Each inbound HTTP request calls fetch(request, env, ctx) with a new ExecutionContext.
entries.notes: A handler that throws gives a plain-text 500 Internal Server Error, not the Cloudflare 1101 error page. A non-Response result fails with Worker fetch handler must return a Response.

entries.name: fetch handler (WorkerEntrypoint class default export)
entries.cloudflare: export default class extends WorkerEntrypoint { fetch(request) } creates an instance per request.
entries.orange: Constructs the class with (ctx, env) for each request and calls its fetch(request).
entries.notes: A class without fetch() loads, and each request fails with Handler does not export a fetch() function., as in workerd.

entries.name: Named WorkerEntrypoint exports
entries.cloudflare: Named entrypoint exports receive fetch, RPC, and connect calls from service bindings, including bindings from other Workers.
entries.orange: Named entrypoints receive fetch, RPC, and connect calls from this Worker's own service bindings and ctx.exports.
entries.notes: Other Workers cannot call them, because cross-Worker service bindings are stubs. js-rpc-test namedServiceBinding times out (cause not checked). extendingEntrypointClasses and testConstructEntrypoint pass.
entries.unverified: The cause of the namedServiceBinding timeout is not checked.

entries.name: scheduled handler
entries.cloudflare: Cron Triggers in triggers.crons call scheduled(controller, env, ctx).
entries.orange: One Orange-internal Rivet Actor holds a Rivet cron job per triggers.crons expression and calls scheduled(controller, env, ctx) on each due minute. /cdn-cgi/local/scheduled and /__scheduled (with --test-scheduled) run it on demand.
entries.notes: orange dev runs crons automatically, where wrangler dev does not. A tick that arrives while the previous run of the same cron still runs is skipped. noRetry() has no effect. Fetcher.scheduled() is not available: http-server-nodejs-test testScheduled fails with The RPC receiver does not implement the method "scheduled". See docs/modules/cron-triggers.mdx.

entries.name: queue handler
entries.cloudflare: Queue consumers in queues.consumers call queue(batch, env, ctx).
entries.orange: The queue actor of each queue in queues.consumers delivers batches to queue(batch, env, ctx), one batch at a time. ack(), retry(), ackAll(), retryAll(), max_retries, retry delays, and dead_letter_queue follow Cloudflare's rules, and delivery is at least once.
entries.notes: max_concurrency is ignored. After an idle period, the first batch waits the whole max_batch_timeout. A queue is shared by name across the orange dev session, so a consumer in another Worker of the session receives the messages. orange dev fails at startup when two Workers declare a consumer for one queue. queue-metadata-test fails because the conformance runner drops its queue binding. See docs/modules/queues.mdx.

entries.name: email handler
entries.cloudflare: Email Routing calls email(message, env, ctx) for inbound mail.
entries.orange: A message POSTed to /cdn-cgi/handler/email, the route that wrangler dev serves, runs email(message, env, ctx): raw MIME with ?from=&to= in the URL, or a SendGrid or Mailgun inbound webhook. message.forward() and message.reply() send through ORANGE_EMAIL_SMTP_URL, and setReject() answers 400.
entries.notes: Email Routing is Cloudflare-only, so mail reaches the Worker only when your email provider's inbound webhook, or a script, POSTs it to the route. orange serve serves the route only when ORANGE_EMAIL_INBOUND_SECRET is set, and a wrong or missing secret gets 401. orange dev serves it without the secret, and checks the secret when it is set. forward() and reply() throw when ORANGE_EMAIL_SMTP_URL is not set. See docs/modules/email.mdx.

entries.name: tail handler
entries.cloudflare: A Tail Worker receives trace events from producer Workers that list it in tail_consumers.
entries.orange: tail_consumers that name the Worker itself or another Worker of the orange dev session get one TraceItem per fetch, service binding fetch(), scheduled, or queue event, with logs, errorInfo, exceptions, outcome, and redacted request details as in workerd.
entries.notes: Durable Object events, JS RPC calls, and alarms are not traced. cpuTime is 0. tests/tail-consumers.test.ts compares a self and a cross-Worker consumer with workerd 1.20260903.1. See docs/modules/tail-workers.mdx.

entries.name: tailStream handler
entries.cloudflare: A streaming Tail Worker receives live trace events from Workers that list it in streaming_tail_consumers.
entries.orange: The Worker loads and the tailStream() handler never runs.
entries.notes: streaming_tail_consumers still fails config load.

entries.name: trace handler
entries.cloudflare: trace is the legacy name of the tail handler.
entries.orange: The Worker loads and the trace() handler never runs.
entries.notes: No trace events are produced.

entries.name: test handler
entries.cloudflare: Cloudflare does not deploy test handlers. workerd calls them only in its own test runner.
entries.orange: The Worker loads and the test() handler never runs.
entries.notes: The conformance runner adapts upstream test handlers itself.

entries.name: connect handler (default export)
entries.cloudflare: connect(socket, env, ctx) handles inbound TCP connections from listeners in the connect config key and from Fetcher.connect().
entries.orange: connect() runs only when this Worker's own service binding or ctx.exports calls connect(). Orange opens no TCP listener.
entries.notes: The connect config key fails config load. connect-handler-test connectHandler and connectHandlerProxy fail because nothing listens on the TCP port. js-rpc-test connectBinding passes.

entries.name: connect handler (named entrypoint)
entries.cloudflare: A named WorkerEntrypoint's connect(socket) handles Fetcher.connect() calls and TCP listeners bound to that entrypoint.
entries.orange: connect(socket) runs for this Worker's own service bindings to the entrypoint. A missing method fails with Handler does not export a connect() function.
entries.notes: Other Workers cannot connect, because cross-Worker service bindings are stubs. connect-handler-test localAddressViaServiceBinding fails because its target service is another Worker.

entries.name: Worker with a connect handler and no fetch handler
entries.cloudflare: A Worker can export only connect() and serve TCP.
entries.orange: The Worker loads. Each HTTP request fails with Handler does not export a fetch() function., as in workerd.
entries.notes: Orange has no inbound TCP connect() events, so the connect handler never runs.

entries.name: Durable Object fetch()
entries.cloudflare: stub.fetch() calls the Durable Object's fetch(request) through the input gate.
entries.orange: stub.fetch() runs the instance fetch(request) as an ordered event inside the input gate.
entries.notes: A class without fetch() fails with Error Handler does not export a fetch() function. A non-Response result fails with TypeError Incorrect type for Promise: the Promise did not resolve to 'Response'. Both match workerd.

entries.name: Durable Object alarm()
entries.cloudflare: alarm(alarmInfo) runs at the time from setAlarm(), with retries on failure.
entries.orange: Runs alarm({ retryCount, isRetry, scheduledTime }) at the stored time, with up to 6 retries.
entries.notes: setAlarm() without an alarm() handler fails with Your Durable Object class must have an alarm() handler in order to call setAlarm(). All 17 synthetic do-alarm tests pass.

entries.name: Durable Object webSocketMessage()
entries.cloudflare: webSocketMessage(ws, message) receives frames on WebSockets accepted with ctx.acceptWebSocket().
entries.orange: Calls webSocketMessage(ws, message) for each frame that is not an auto-response, as an input-gated event.
entries.notes: A missing method silently drops the event, like workerd. The handler runs on the shared Node thread, so a synchronous loop cannot be stopped by the event timeout.

entries.name: Durable Object webSocketClose()
entries.cloudflare: webSocketClose(ws, code, reason, wasClean) runs when a hibernatable WebSocket closes.
entries.orange: Calls webSocketClose(ws, code, reason, wasClean) once. The socket stays listed until the handler settles.
entries.notes: A client's close code can be lost in the Rivet gateway: in the recorded lifecycle probe, a clean client close reached webSocketClose as 1001, not 1000. A missing method silently drops the event.

entries.name: Durable Object webSocketError()
entries.cloudflare: webSocketError(ws, error) runs when a hibernatable WebSocket fails.
entries.orange: Calls webSocketError(ws, error) once and releases the socket.
entries.notes: No conformance test triggers a WebSocket error.
entries.unverified: No test drives the error path. The claim is read from code.

entries.name: Durable Object connect()
entries.cloudflare: stub.connect() opens a TCP-style socket to the Durable Object's connect() handler.
entries.orange: stub.connect() throws DurableObjectStub.connect is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: A connect() method on a Durable Object class never runs.
entries.unverified: Whether Cloudflare production exposes Durable Object connect() is not checked.

entries.name: caches global
entries.cloudflare: The caches global gives access to the Cache API for the zone.
entries.orange: A CacheStorage backed by one internal Rivet Actor per cache name (SQLite), with Miniflare's freshness rules. Entries survive orange dev restarts. ORANGE_CACHE=off restores the workers.dev no-op.
entries.notes: One local cache, not one per data center. Several ranges get the whole body with 200. The per-request call limit is not enforced. Upstream cache-test matchOperations and deleteOperations depend on workerd's mock cache backend.

entries.name: caches.default
entries.cloudflare: The default cache for the zone. match(), put(), and delete() read and write the edge cache.
entries.orange: A Cache stored in the openorange:cache actor named default. put() validates and stores fresh responses, match() returns HIT, 304, 206, or 416 responses, and delete() returns whether a live entry was removed.
entries.notes: See caches.

entries.name: caches.open()
entries.cloudflare: Opens a named cache in the zone.
entries.orange: Resolves to a Cache stored in the openorange:cache actor named named:<name>. A name of 1024 characters or more throws TypeError: Cache name is too long.
entries.notes: See caches.

entries.name: Cache class
entries.cloudflare: The Cache global is the class of caches.default and of caches opened with caches.open().
entries.orange: Exists. new Cache() throws TypeError: Illegal constructor, as in workerd.
entries.notes: See caches.

entries.name: CacheStorage class
entries.cloudflare: The CacheStorage global is the class of caches.
entries.orange: Exists. new CacheStorage() throws TypeError: Illegal constructor, as in workerd.
entries.notes: See caches.

entries.name: Worker ctx.waitUntil()
entries.cloudflare: Keeps the invocation alive until the promise settles, after the response is sent.
entries.orange: Tracks each promise. The runtime drains them after the handler returns or throws.
entries.notes: Promises added while draining are also awaited. Orange has no 30 second post-response limit.
entries.unverified: The missing post-response time limit is read from code, not tested.

entries.name: ctx.passThroughOnException()
entries.cloudflare: Forwards the request to the origin when the Worker throws.
entries.orange: A no-op. An exception after the call still fails the request with a 500 response.
entries.notes: Orange has no origin to fall back to. Local workerd with no next service also answers the exception with an error.

entries.name: ctx.cache
entries.cloudflare: Gives cache controls, such as ctx.cache.purge(), on cache-enabled Workers.
entries.orange: Reading ctx.cache throws NotSupportedError ExecutionContext.cache is not implemented.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Worker ctx.abort()
entries.cloudflare: Aborts the current invocation with a reason.
entries.orange: Disposes the RPC stubs the invocation owns, then throws the reason, which fails the invocation.
entries.notes: Workerd also terminates the running JavaScript at once. Node.js cannot, so code that catches the thrown reason keeps running. Durable Object ctx.abort() is separate. js-rpc-test disposal passes.

entries.name: ctx.props
entries.cloudflare: Holds the props that a service binding or ctx.exports call bound to the entrypoint.
entries.orange: Holds the props of a same-Worker service binding or ctx.exports call. Top-level HTTP requests get undefined.
entries.notes: ctx-props-test-disabled fails: with the legacy nonclass_entrypoint_reuses_ctx_across_invocations flag, workerd returns {} and Orange returns undefined.
entries.unverified: What Cloudflare returns for ctx.props on a top-level request without that flag is not checked.

entries.name: ctx.access
entries.cloudflare: Holds Cloudflare Access identity for the request when Access protects the Worker.
entries.orange: Always undefined, like local workerd.
entries.notes: Orange has no Access integration, so Access-protected routes cannot read the identity.

entries.name: ctx.tracing
entries.cloudflare: The user tracing API. enterSpan() is a no-op outside a traced request.
entries.orange: ctx.tracing is a no-op tracer. Callbacks run with a span whose isTraced is false, and errors propagate.
entries.notes: No spans are recorded. DurableObjectState has no tracing, as in workerd.

entries.name: ctx.mapVirtualHost()
entries.cloudflare: Assigns a stable virtual host name to a Fetcher for a port. workerd exposes it under the experimental flag.
entries.orange: Assigns a stable <id>.workers.alt:<port> host and keeps the first port per Fetcher.
entries.notes: Works with connect() through the mapped host.

entries.name: ctx.version
entries.cloudflare: Version information on ctx. workerd exposes it only under the experimental enable_version_api flag.
entries.orange: Not present. ctx.version reads undefined.
entries.notes: Cloudflare does not deploy experimental flags. Use the version_metadata binding instead.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers WorkerEntrypoint
entries.cloudflare: Base class for default and named entrypoints. The runtime passes ctx and env to the constructor.
entries.orange: Base class that stores ctx and env. A class default export gets a new instance for each request.
entries.notes: Each event method needs a handler entry. Orange dispatches fetch, connect, and RPC methods.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers DurableObject
entries.cloudflare: Base class for Durable Object classes. Extending it enables RPC.
entries.orange: Base class that Orange requires for Durable Object classes and RPC.
entries.notes: Durable Object behavior is in the Durable Objects category.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers RpcTarget
entries.cloudflare: Marks a class whose instances travel over RPC as stubs instead of being copied.
entries.orange: Marks the class for both Orange RPC systems. Instances travel as stubs that expose class members only.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers RpcStub
entries.cloudflare: new RpcStub(value) wraps a local object or function as a disposable RPC stub.
entries.orange: Constructs a disposable stub with dup() and Symbol.dispose.
entries.notes: See the JS RPC entries for ownership and disposal.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers RpcPromise
entries.cloudflare: Class of the promise an RPC call returns. It supports pipelining.
entries.orange: Exported for instanceof checks. RPC calls return instances.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers RpcProperty
entries.cloudflare: Class of a pipelined property read on a stub.
entries.orange: Exported for instanceof checks. Property reads on stubs return instances.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers ServiceStub
entries.cloudflare: Class of a service binding stub (Fetcher).
entries.orange: Exported. Service stubs from bindings and ctx.exports are instances.
entries.notes: Only same-Worker service stubs exist in Orange.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers waitUntil()
entries.cloudflare: Registers background work on the current invocation without ctx.
entries.orange: Adds the promise to the current execution context. Outside a request, throws the workerd Disallowed operation called within global scope error.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: No upstream test calls the module-level waitUntil().

entries.name: cloudflare:workers withEnv()
entries.cloudflare: Runs a function with an overridden importable env.
entries.orange: Runs the function with the override in an AsyncLocalStorage scope, with workerd's null and non-object rules.
entries.notes: The importable env object itself is in the Bindings category.
entries.unverified: importable-env-test fails at load for an unrelated KV binding, so no passing test covers withEnv().

entries.name: cloudflare:workers withExports()
entries.cloudflare: Runs a function with an overridden importable exports object.
entries.orange: Runs the function with the override in an AsyncLocalStorage scope.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers withEnvAndExports()
entries.cloudflare: Runs a function with both env and exports overridden.
entries.orange: Nests withEnv() and withExports().
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: No upstream test calls it.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers restore()
entries.cloudflare: Restores persistent stubs. Requires the allow_irrevocable_stub_storage flag.
entries.orange: Exported so imports link. Calling it throws cloudflare:workers restore() is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: persistent-stubs-test fails 0/20.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers WorkflowEntrypoint
entries.cloudflare: Base class for Workflow classes.
entries.orange: Exported as a base class that stores ctx and env. A Workflow binding constructs the class for each run of an instance and calls run(event, step).
entries.notes: See binding-workflows.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers cache
entries.cloudflare: Module-level proxy for the current request's ctx.cache.
entries.orange: Not exported. A Worker that imports it fails at load with The requested module does not provide an export named 'cache'.
entries.notes: cloudflare:workers resolves to Orange's ES module, so a missing named export fails when the Worker module links. The conformance classifier matches this error.
entries.unverified: Not run against Orange for this export. The failure follows from ES module linking.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers tracing
entries.cloudflare: Module-level user tracing API.
entries.orange: Exported. It is the same no-op tracer as ctx.tracing.
entries.notes: No spans are recorded.

entries.name: cloudflare:workers abortIsolate
entries.cloudflare: Aborts the isolate with a reason.
entries.orange: Not exported. A Worker that imports it fails at load with The requested module does not provide an export named 'abortIsolate'.
entries.notes: cloudflare:workers resolves to Orange's ES module, so a missing named export fails when the Worker module links. The conformance classifier matches this error.
entries.unverified: Not run against Orange for this export. The failure follows from ES module linking.

entries.name: cloudflare:node httpServerHandler()
entries.cloudflare: Makes a fetch handler that routes requests to a node:http server by port.
entries.orange: Routes requests to node:http servers registered by port, with workerd's error text for an unknown port.
entries.notes: node:http server behavior is in the Node.js compat category.

entries.name: cloudflare:node handleAsNodeRequest()
entries.cloudflare: Sends one fetch request to a node:http server by port.
entries.orange: Routes the request to the node:http server registered on the port, with workerd's error text for an unknown port.
entries.notes: node:http server behavior is in the Node.js compat category.

entries.name: cloudflare:email module
entries.cloudflare: Exports EmailMessage for send_email bindings and email handlers.
entries.orange: Exports EmailMessage with from and to, as workerd does.
entries.notes: Sending needs a Send Email binding with ORANGE_EMAIL_SMTP_URL set; without it, the binding's calls throw. Workers that only build messages, such as the agents SDK, load and run.

entries.name: cloudflare:workflows module
entries.cloudflare: Exports NonRetryableError for Workflows.
entries.orange: Exports NonRetryableError, as workerd does.
entries.notes: A step that throws an error named NonRetryableError stops retrying, as in workerd.

entries.name: cloudflare:pipelines module
entries.cloudflare: Exports PipelineTransformationEntrypoint for Pipelines.
entries.orange: Exports PipelineTransformationEntrypoint as a WorkerEntrypoint subclass.
entries.notes: Orange delivers no pipeline batches.

entries.name: cloudflare:ai module
entries.cloudflare: Exports Workers AI helper types and errors.
entries.orange: Exports the same names as workerd. The error classes work. Constructing Ai, AiGateway, AutoRAG, or ToMarkdownService throws NotSupportedError.
entries.notes: The ai binding works through an OpenAI-compatible provider. See binding-workers-ai.

entries.name: cloudflare:vectorize module
entries.cloudflare: Exports Vectorize constants such as DistanceMetric.
entries.orange: Exports the same constants as workerd.
entries.notes: Vectorize bindings are stubs.

entries.name: cloudflare:br module
entries.cloudflare: Exports BrowserRendering helpers.
entries.orange: Exports BrowserRendering, which forwards fetch() like workerd.
entries.notes: The Browser Rendering binding it wraps needs ORANGE_BROWSER_CDP_URL. See binding-browser-rendering.

entries.name: Unresolvable imports
entries.cloudflare: workerd fails an unresolvable import, or a require() of a module with top-level await, only when the importing module evaluates.
entries.orange: The bundler replaces those imports with modules that throw workerd's error text and prints a [bundle-warning] for each one.
entries.notes: cloudflare: imports without an Orange module are not deferred. A require() of a module with unsettled top-level await hangs instead of throwing.

entries.name: WebAssembly module imports (.wasm)
entries.cloudflare: Wrangler bundles .wasm imports as WebAssembly.Module values.
entries.orange: Imports that match a CompiledWasm rule (by default **/*.wasm and **/*.wasm?module) load as a WebAssembly.Module, as in Wrangler.
entries.notes: The module bytes are inlined in the bundle. Source phase imports of Wasm still fail to bundle.

entries.name: Web File System API
entries.cloudflare: Only behind workerd's experimental enable_web_file_system flag. Cloudflare does not deploy experimental flags.
entries.orange: Not implemented. The upstream files are scored as Not supported.
entries.notes: The webfs files stay in the total as failures.

entries.name: new_module_registry (unbundled modules)
entries.cloudflare: Opt-in flag that resolves unbundled modules as URLs at runtime.
entries.orange: Orange always bundles the Worker.
entries.notes: The upstream file is scored as Not supported.

entries.name: workerd:unsafe module
entries.cloudflare: workerd:unsafe exists only in workerd test or experimental configurations.
entries.orange: Not available. The import fails when it evaluates with No such module "workerd:unsafe".
entries.notes: 19 tests need it and are excluded from the score.

entries.name: workerd:unsafe-eval module
entries.cloudflare: workerd:unsafe-eval exists only in workerd test or experimental configurations.
entries.orange: Not available. The import fails when it evaluates with No such module "workerd:unsafe-eval".
entries.notes: 1 test needs it and is excluded from the score.

entries.name: workerd:rtti module
entries.cloudflare: workerd:rtti exists only in workerd test or experimental configurations.
entries.orange: Not available. The import fails when it evaluates with No such module "workerd:rtti".
entries.notes: rtti-test imports it and fails at load.

entries.name: gc() global
entries.cloudflare: gc() exists only in workerd test builds.
entries.orange: Not defined.
entries.notes: Tests that call gc() are excluded from the score.

entries.name: Global scope isolation
entries.cloudflare: Each Worker runs in its own V8 isolate. The runtime's own code does not share the global scope.
entries.orange: Worker code and the Orange runtime share one Node.js realm. Orange installs the Cloudflare globals on that realm.
entries.notes: Patching a shared global, such as Promise or a Node.js built-in, also changes the runtime. global-scope-test passes 22/22.

entries.name: process global
entries.cloudflare: With nodejs_compat, each Worker has its own workerd process object.
entries.orange: Worker code shares the host Node.js process object with the runtime.
entries.notes: process.exit() stops the runtime. process-nodejs-test fails 0/24 and process-exit-test fails at load.
entries.unverified: Why each of the 24 process-nodejs-test cases fails is not checked. They fail at file load.

entries.name: self
entries.cloudflare: self refers to the global scope.
entries.orange: self is globalThis.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: WorkerGlobalScope class
entries.cloudflare: The class of the global scope.
entries.orange: The global is a placeholder that throws Cloudflare global WorkerGlobalScope is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: globalThis instanceof WorkerGlobalScope throws instead of returning true.

entries.name: origin global
entries.cloudflare: The origin global property.
entries.orange: The global is a placeholder that throws Cloudflare global origin is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Global addEventListener()
entries.cloudflare: Adds a listener on the global scope for error, unhandledrejection, and rejectionhandled events.
entries.orange: One process-wide EventTarget method exposed as a global.
entries.notes: Service Worker fetch listeners do not handle requests. See the FetchEvent entry.

entries.name: Global removeEventListener()
entries.cloudflare: Removes a listener from the global scope.
entries.orange: One process-wide EventTarget method exposed as a global.
entries.notes: Service Worker fetch listeners do not handle requests. See the FetchEvent entry.

entries.name: Global dispatchEvent()
entries.cloudflare: Dispatches an event on the global scope.
entries.orange: One process-wide EventTarget method exposed as a global.
entries.notes: Service Worker fetch listeners do not handle requests. See the FetchEvent entry.

entries.name: FetchEvent and Service Worker syntax
entries.cloudflare: Service Worker syntax Workers handle requests with addEventListener("fetch").
entries.orange: FetchEvent is a throwing placeholder. A Worker without a default export fails at load with Worker entrypoint must have a default object export.
entries.notes: Only ES module Workers run on Orange.
entries.workaround: Convert the Worker to ES module syntax with a default export.

entries.name: ExtendableEvent class
entries.cloudflare: The base class of Service Worker events. User code cannot construct it.
entries.orange: The global is a placeholder that throws Cloudflare global ExtendableEvent is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: events-test extendableEventNotConstructable passes because the placeholder throws on construct.

entries.name: ScheduledEvent class
entries.cloudflare: The event class for Service Worker scheduled events.
entries.orange: The global is a placeholder that throws Cloudflare global ScheduledEvent is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: Scheduled handlers are in the Worker handlers category.

entries.name: TailEvent class
entries.cloudflare: The event class for Service Worker tail events.
entries.orange: The global is a placeholder that throws Cloudflare global TailEvent is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: Tail handlers are in the Worker handlers category.

entries.name: Body class
entries.cloudflare: The Body mixin class shared by Request and Response.
entries.orange: The global is a placeholder that throws Cloudflare global Body is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: Request and Response bodies work. Only the Body global is missing.

entries.name: I/O at global scope
entries.cloudflare: Asynchronous I/O, timers, and random values at module scope throw Disallowed operation called within global scope.
entries.orange: fetch(), setTimeout(), and similar calls at module scope run. Only cloudflare:workers waitUntil() throws the workerd error.
entries.notes: A Worker that does I/O at module scope works on Orange and fails to deploy or load on Cloudflare.
entries.unverified: No conformance test covers module-scope I/O on Orange. The only test, new-module-registry-test noTopLevelIo, is not supported.

entries.name: eval() restriction
entries.cloudflare: eval() throws EvalError Code generation from strings disallowed for this context, except through the unsafe_eval binding.
entries.orange: eval() runs at any time, like in Node.js.
entries.notes: Code that works on Orange can fail on Cloudflare. worker-test testStartupEval and unsafe-test basics fail on this.

entries.name: new Function() restriction
entries.cloudflare: new Function() throws EvalError Code generation from strings disallowed for this context, except through the unsafe_eval binding.
entries.orange: new Function() runs at any time, like in Node.js.

entries.orange: Request deep-clones cf and keeps it on request.cf, then sends nothing from it.
entries.notes: cacheControl conflicts with cacheTtl or the cache option throw as in workerd. cf-cache-control-test: 4 of 4 pass. Each cf option is listed in its own entry.

entries.name: cf.cacheTtl
entries.cloudflare: Sets the edge cache TTL for the subrequest response.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: Orange has no edge cache, so subrequest responses are never cached. They do not go through the Cache API either, as in wrangler dev.

entries.name: cf.cacheTtlByStatus
entries.cloudflare: Sets edge cache TTLs per response status range.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: Orange has no edge cache, so responses are never cached.

entries.name: cf.cacheEverything
entries.cloudflare: Caches every response, not only static file types.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: Orange has no edge cache, so subrequest responses are never cached. They do not go through the Cache API either, as in wrangler dev.

entries.name: cf.cacheKey
entries.cloudflare: Sets a custom edge cache key.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: Orange has no edge cache, so responses are never cached.

entries.name: cf.cacheTags
entries.cloudflare: Tags the cached response for purge by tag.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: Orange has no edge cache, so responses are never cached.

entries.name: cf.cacheControl
entries.cloudflare: Sends explicit Cache-Control directives to the edge cache.
entries.orange: Validated against cacheTtl and the cache option, then ignored.
entries.notes: Orange has no edge cache, so responses are never cached.

entries.name: cf.image
entries.cloudflare: Resizes and converts images with Image Resizing.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The response is the origin's response, unchanged.

entries.name: cf.polish
entries.cloudflare: Optimizes images with Polish.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The response is the origin's response, unchanged.

entries.name: cf.minify
entries.cloudflare: Minifies JavaScript, CSS, and HTML in the response.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The response is the origin's response, unchanged.

entries.name: cf.mirage
entries.cloudflare: Turns on Mirage image loading.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The response is the origin's response, unchanged.

entries.name: cf.scrapeShield
entries.cloudflare: Turns ScrapeShield features on or off.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The response is the origin's response, unchanged.

entries.name: cf.apps
entries.cloudflare: Turns Cloudflare Apps injection on or off.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The response is the origin's response, unchanged.

entries.name: cf.resolveOverride
entries.cloudflare: Sends the request to a different hostname in the same zone.
entries.orange: Ignored. The request goes to the origin unchanged and no edge feature runs.
entries.notes: The request goes to the hostname in the URL.

entries.name: Request cache option
entries.cloudflare: cache accepts no-store and no-cache. Other modes throw Unsupported cache mode. Before the cache_option_enabled flag, Request has no cache property.
entries.orange: cache is always present. no-store and no-cache go to undici. Other modes, such as default, are accepted without an error and read back as undefined.
entries.notes: http-test cacheMode fails because 'cache' in Request.prototype is true without the flag.
entries.unverified: Checked against undici 8.10.2 directly for the accepted default mode. What undici sends for no-store and no-cache is not checked.

entries.name: Incoming request.signal
entries.cloudflare: With enable_request_signal, request.signal aborts when the client disconnects.
entries.orange: request.signal always aborts when the client aborts or closes the connection before the response ends.
entries.notes: No compat flag is needed. request-signal-enabled: 5 of 6 pass. abortedRequestDoesNotAbortSubrequest fails. request_signal_passthrough is not honored: requestPassedOverRpcIncludesSignal fails.

entries.name: fetch() with an AbortSignal
entries.cloudflare: init.signal cancels an in-flight subrequest.
entries.orange: Passes signal to undici, which cancels the request.
entries.notes: abortable-fetch-test: 6 of 7 pass. requestAbortSignal fails because new Request('') throws. See fetch-request-relative-url.

entries.name: Request with an empty or relative URL
entries.cloudflare: new Request('') succeeds and gives a Request with an empty URL.
entries.orange: new Request('') throws TypeError: Failed to parse URL from.
entries.notes: undici requires an absolute URL.

entries.name: Outbound WebSocket through fetch()
entries.cloudflare: fetch() with Upgrade: websocket returns a 101 response whose webSocket property is the client end.
entries.orange: fetch() rejects with TypeError: fetch failed, caused by invalid upgrade header from undici.
entries.notes: The error does not say that Orange lacks the feature.
entries.unverified: The undici error was reproduced with undici 8.10.2 directly, not through a running Worker.

entries.name: Outbound new WebSocket(url)
entries.cloudflare: new WebSocket(url) opens a client WebSocket. Inside a Durable Object, the connection waits for the output gate.
entries.orange: Extends Node's built-in WebSocket and connects at once.
entries.notes: Connection setup does not wait for the Durable Object output gate. websocket-constructor-test: 18 of 18 pass.

entries.name: Inbound WebSocket upgrade
entries.cloudflare: A fetch handler accepts a WebSocket by returning new Response(null, { status: 101, webSocket }).
entries.orange: The runtime calls fetch for the upgrade request and couples the returned WebSocketPair end to the network socket.
entries.notes: A non-101 response is written back as a plain HTTP response. A selected subprotocol that the client did not offer fails the upgrade. The upgrade request has no request.signal tied to the client.

entries.name: fetch() of data: URLs
entries.cloudflare: fetch() decodes data: URLs locally.
entries.orange: undici decodes data: URLs locally.
entries.notes: data-url-fetch-test: 2 of 2 pass.

entries.name: connect() to a ctx.mapVirtualHost() host
entries.cloudflare: ctx.mapVirtualHost(fetcher, port) returns a .workers.alt host. connect() to that host goes through the fetcher.
entries.orange: Returns a random <hex>.workers.alt:<port> host per fetcher. connect() to it calls the fetcher's connect().
entries.notes: Only connect() uses the mapping. fetch() to that host goes to undici and fails DNS.
entries.unverified: fetch() to a mapped host is read from code and not run.

entries.name: cloudflare:sockets connect()
entries.cloudflare: TCP sockets leave through Cloudflare's network. Port 25 and Cloudflare IP ranges are blocked.
entries.orange: Sockets connect directly from the host with node:net. No port or address is blocked.
entries.notes: Inside a Durable Object, connect() to the network does not wait for the output gate. Egress IP and network policy are the host's.

entries.name: connect() with secureTransport: "on"
entries.cloudflare: Opens a TLS connection with the hostname as SNI.
entries.orange: Opens a node:tls connection with servername set to the hostname.
entries.notes: Invalid values throw Unsupported value in secureTransport socket option.
entries.unverified: No saved test opens a real TLS socket through cloudflare:sockets.

entries.name: socket.startTls()
entries.cloudflare: Upgrades a socket opened with secureTransport: "starttls" to TLS.
entries.orange: Upgrades the connection with node:tls and returns a new Socket. Misuse throws workerd's error messages.
entries.notes: transferredSocketCannotStartTls passes.
entries.unverified: No saved test runs a full STARTTLS handshake.

entries.name: connect() with allowHalfOpen
entries.cloudflare: allowHalfOpen: false closes the write side when the peer sends EOF. true keeps it open.
entries.orange: Applies the same rule on top of a half-open node:net socket.
entries.notes: Both transferred-socket half-open tests pass.

entries.name: Streaming request bodies
entries.cloudflare: A ReadableStream body streams to the origin. A FixedLengthStream or expectedLength body is sent with Content-Length.
entries.orange: Streams the body through undici with duplex: "half". Global fetch() ignores expectedLength and sends chunked encoding.
entries.notes: Service binding fetch() sets Content-Length from expectedLength. http-test test fails on a Transfer-Encoding check.
entries.unverified: The chunked encoding on global fetch() is read from code and not run against an origin.

entries.name: Response.json()
entries.cloudflare: Response.json(value, init) builds a JSON response.
entries.orange: Builds the response with undici and accepts a Response as init.
entries.notes: response-json: 6 of 6 pass.

entries.name: Headers.getSetCookie()
entries.cloudflare: Returns each Set-Cookie value.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: Responses written to the client keep each Set-Cookie header separate.
entries.unverified: No saved test covers getSetCookie() or getAll().

entries.name: Headers.getAll()
entries.cloudflare: Works only for Set-Cookie.
entries.orange: Same. getAll() with another name throws TypeError.
entries.notes: Responses written to the client keep each Set-Cookie header separate.
entries.unverified: No saved test covers getSetCookie() or getAll().

entries.name: Automatic response compression (Content-Encoding)
entries.cloudflare: When a Worker returns a Response with Content-Encoding: gzip or br, the runtime compresses the body.
entries.orange: Compresses bodies whose Content-Encoding is exactly gzip or br, for Worker and Durable Object responses, and drops the stale Content-Length. Other codings are sent unchanged.
entries.notes: Matches workerd's automatic encodeBody mode.

entries.name: Automatic decompression of fetch() responses
entries.cloudflare: fetch() decodes gzip and br response bodies.
entries.orange: undici decodes gzip, deflate, and br response bodies.
entries.notes: Unlike workerd, deflate bodies are also decoded.
entries.unverified: Relies on undici defaults. Not run.

entries.name: encodeBody: "manual" on Response
entries.cloudflare: encodeBody: "manual" sends an already compressed body as is.
entries.orange: encodeBody: "manual" sends the bytes unchanged. A Response passed as init keeps the mode, and clone() resets it to automatic.
entries.notes: A service binding caller reads a manually encoded body decoded.

entries.name: encodeResponseBody on Request
entries.cloudflare: encodeResponseBody: "manual" keeps the response body compressed.
entries.orange: new Request(url, { encodeResponseBody }) throws NotSupportedError: encodeResponseBody is not implemented yet.
entries.notes: Any value throws, including "automatic".

entries.name: Plain class Durable Objects
entries.cloudflare: A class that does not extend DurableObject works for fetch(), alarms, and WebSockets. RPC to it fails unless js_rpc is set.
entries.orange: Same. RPC to a plain class fails with workerd's message: The receiving Durable Object does not support RPC, because its class was not declared with `extends DurableObject`.
entries.notes: Orange ignores the js_rpc flag, so a plain class never accepts RPC.

entries.name: DurableObject base class
entries.cloudflare: `import { DurableObject } from "cloudflare:workers"`. The constructor stores ctx and env, and the class enables RPC.
entries.orange: Same. The base class sets this.ctx and this.env and brands the prototype for RPC.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Object constructor
entries.cloudflare: The class constructor runs once per object instance, with ctx and env, before the first event.
entries.orange: Same. Each Rivet actor generation constructs exactly one instance, with a fresh ctx and env, before any event runs.
entries.notes: Instance fields do not survive sleep, as on Cloudflare.

entries.name: Idle eviction and sleep
entries.cloudflare: An idle object is evicted from memory after some time without events. Its storage stays.
entries.orange: An idle object sleeps after 10 seconds without events (Rivet sleepTimeout 10_000). The next event constructs a new instance.
entries.notes: Orange uses workerd's 10 second hibernation cadence for every idle object. Code that keeps state in instance fields loses it sooner than on Cloudflare.
entries.unverified: Cloudflare's exact production eviction delay is not measured here.

entries.name: namespace.idFromName()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a deterministic DurableObjectId for a name. The id has a name property.
entries.orange: Same. The id is deterministic within one deployment and class. The id bytes differ from Cloudflare's.
entries.notes: Ids are local to Orange and are not interchangeable with Cloudflare ids.

entries.name: namespace.idFromString()
entries.cloudflare: Parses a 64-digit hex id. It rejects malformed ids and ids from another class. The name is not restored.
entries.orange: Same. It validates the hex form, the class namespace, and the jurisdiction, and drops the name.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: namespace.newUniqueId()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a random id. The jurisdiction option restricts the id to a jurisdiction.
entries.orange: Same. Ids use cryptographic randomness. The jurisdiction option is validated and stored on the id.
entries.notes: A jurisdiction is metadata only. Orange stores all data on the local host.

entries.name: namespace.get()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a stub for an id. Options locationHint and routingMode are accepted.
entries.orange: Same. The stub is lazy and does not contact the actor until the first call. Invalid options throw TypeError.
entries.notes: locationHint has no effect. See do-location-hint.

entries.name: namespace.getByName()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a stub for idFromName(name) in one call.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: namespace.jurisdiction()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a namespace whose ids are restricted to one jurisdiction. null means no restriction.
entries.orange: Same. A restricted namespace rejects ids from another jurisdiction. null acts like no jurisdiction.
entries.notes: A jurisdiction is metadata only. Orange stores all data on the local host.

entries.name: id.toString()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the id as 64 lowercase hex digits.
entries.orange: Same format.
entries.notes: The digits differ from Cloudflare's for the same name.

entries.name: id.equals()
entries.cloudflare: Compares two ids by value. The name does not matter.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: id.name and ctx.id.name
entries.cloudflare: id.name is the name passed to idFromName(). ctx.id.name keeps it inside the object, also in alarms after eviction.
entries.orange: Same. Orange keeps the name in the actor's SQLite, so it survives sleep, alarm wake-ups, and deleteAll().
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: id.jurisdiction
entries.cloudflare: The jurisdiction of the id, or undefined.
entries.orange: Same. idFromString() restores it.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: stub.id
entries.cloudflare: The stub's Durable Object id. id and name are the only own enumerable keys.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: stub.name
entries.cloudflare: The name the stub was made from, for getByName() and idFromName() stubs.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: stub.fetch()
entries.cloudflare: Sends an HTTP request to the object's fetch() handler. WebSocket upgrades work.
entries.orange: Same, through a private Rivet route. The method, headers, and cf of the request, and the headers and status text of the object's response, cross in private heads. Gateway headers and CORS never reach the Worker, and OPTIONS reaches the object.
entries.notes: RivetKit's gateway client reads the whole request body into memory before it forwards it. Client-sent private head headers are dropped at the inbound edge.

entries.name: Stub RPC method calls
entries.cloudflare: stub.method(args) calls a public method of the class. Arguments and results use the RPC serializer, including stubs, functions, streams, Request, and Response.
entries.orange: Same API, over Cap'n Web through Rivet. Calls keep E-order per stub. Errors keep name, message, and custom properties.
entries.notes: Values follow workerd's RPC serializer, including Blob, Response.error(), DOMException, and boxed primitives. File, FormData, URL, AbortSignal, and other classes fail with workerd's DataCloneError message. Durable Object stubs cannot be sent over RPC (see do-stub-transfer-over-rpc). An error that the object throws rejects only that call; see do-stub-broken-after-error. Calls run on the single Node thread.

entries.name: Stub RPC property access
entries.cloudflare: Awaiting stub.prop reads a property or getter of the class over RPC.
entries.orange: Same. Own instance properties are rejected, as on Cloudflare.
entries.notes: Reading the property does not wake the object. Awaiting it does.
entries.unverified: namedActorBinding is the closest saved test. No saved test reads a getter on a Durable Object stub directly.

entries.name: RpcPromise pipelining
entries.cloudflare: Calls on an unresolved RpcPromise (stub.a().b()) are pipelined in one round trip.
entries.orange: The result is correct, but each pipelined call waits for its parent result and then sends a new call.
entries.notes: Extra round trips per pipelined step. map() and onRpcBroken() on the promise read as undefined.

entries.name: stub.connect()
entries.cloudflare: Opens a TCP-style socket to the object's connect() handler.
entries.orange: Calling it throws DurableObjectStub.connect is not implemented by OpenOrange.
entries.notes: Service binding connect() works. Only Durable Object stubs lack it.

entries.name: Stub reuse across requests
entries.cloudflare: A stub belongs to the request that created it. Using it from another request throws Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request.
entries.orange: A stub has no request owner. A stub kept in a global works from any later request.
entries.notes: Code that works on Orange can fail on Cloudflare. Service binding RPC objects do enforce request ownership.
entries.unverified: Found by code reading. No saved test covers a Durable Object stub used from a second request.

entries.name: Sending a Durable Object stub over RPC
entries.cloudflare: A stub can be an RPC argument or result. It arrives as a service stub (Fetcher).
entries.orange: Fails with DataCloneError Could not serialize object of type "LazyDurableObjectStub". This type does not support serialization.
entries.notes: Pass the id string and call get() on the other side.
entries.workaround: Send id.toString() and rebuild the stub with namespace.idFromString() and get().

entries.name: Stub broken after a failed call
entries.cloudflare: After a call through a stub fails because the object reset, later calls on that stub fail with the same error.
entries.orange: Same. A reset or a transport failure poisons the stub's ordering lane, and the error carries durableObjectReset: true after a reset. An error that the object's own code throws rejects only that call, as in workerd. get() returns a new working stub.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Input gate
entries.cloudflare: While a storage call or critical section runs, no other event reaches the object. This includes new requests and I/O results for events already running.
entries.orange: New events (fetch, RPC, alarms, WebSocket events) wait while a critical section holds the gate. Storage calls finish synchronously, so they never open a gap.
entries.notes: Orange gates only event admission. A fetch() result or timer of an event that is already running can resume during another event's critical section. During an open storage.transaction(), such code that calls synchronous storage throws Synchronous storage cannot run while another event's storage.transaction() is open.
entries.unverified: The resume-during-critical-section gap is found by code reading. No saved test covers it.

entries.name: Output gate: event results and errors
entries.cloudflare: A response, RPC result, or thrown error leaves the object only after the writes made before it are durable.
entries.orange: Same. Each event waits for the output gate before its result or error is returned. If the commit fails, the object resets and the caller gets the reset error.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Output gate: outbound fetch()
entries.cloudflare: A fetch() from the object is sent only after earlier writes are durable.
entries.orange: Same. Global fetch() waits on the object's output gate before it sends.
entries.notes: Tested end to end with the Rivet engine stopped between the write and the fetch.

entries.name: Output gate: service binding calls
entries.cloudflare: A service binding fetch() or RPC call from the object leaves after earlier writes are durable.
entries.orange: Same. Service fetch(), RPC, and connect() wait on the output gate.
entries.notes: The callee entrypoint is constructed before the gate opens. It runs only after it opens.

entries.name: Output gate: Durable Object stub calls
entries.cloudflare: A fetch() or RPC call through another object's stub leaves after earlier writes are durable.
entries.orange: Same. Stub calls wait on the output gate and keep E-order.
entries.notes: Verified by code. The end-to-end output gate test covers service RPC, not stub calls.

entries.name: Output gate: RPC session frames
entries.cloudflare: Results of calls on stubs or targets that an object returned are outputs of that object and wait for its writes.
entries.orange: Same. The object side and the caller side of the private RPC WebSocket hold each outgoing frame on the output gate, in order.
entries.notes: Verified by code. No end-to-end test.

entries.name: Output gate: WebSocket send()
entries.cloudflare: Each ws.send() from the object leaves after the writes made before it are durable, in send order.
entries.orange: Same for WebSocketPair sockets and outbound WebSocket clients. A failed commit drops the held frame and every later one.
entries.notes: Tested end to end with an outbound WebSocket client.

entries.name: Output gate: WebSocket close()
entries.cloudflare: ws.close() from the object waits for earlier writes, after earlier frames.
entries.orange: Same. close() goes through the same ordered output queue as send().
entries.notes: Verified by code. The end-to-end test covers send(), not close().

entries.name: Output gate: allowUnconfirmed writes
entries.cloudflare: A write with allowUnconfirmed: true does not hold outgoing messages.
entries.orange: Same for put(), delete(), setAlarm(), and deleteAlarm(). deleteAll() ignores the option, as in workerd.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Output gate gap: streamed body chunks
entries.cloudflare: Response and request body chunks that stream after the headers also wait for earlier writes.
entries.orange: Only the start of the request or response waits. Chunks written to the body stream later leave at once.
entries.notes: A peer can see a chunk that depends on a write that is later lost in a crash.
entries.unverified: Found by code reading: no output gate wait in the body stream path. No test covers it.

entries.name: Output gate gap: outbound new WebSocket() setup
entries.cloudflare: Opening an outbound WebSocket from the object waits for earlier writes.
entries.orange: new WebSocket(url) connects at once. Only its later send() and close() calls wait.
entries.notes: The handshake request can reach the peer before earlier writes are durable.
entries.unverified: Found by code reading. No test covers it.

entries.name: Output gate gap: code outside the object's async context
entries.cloudflare: All output of the object waits for its writes, whatever callback runs it.
entries.orange: Orange finds the object's gate through AsyncLocalStorage. Output from callbacks that a raw Node.js API or a Cap'n Web session runs outside that context is not held.
entries.notes: Output from such callbacks can leave before earlier writes are durable.
entries.unverified: Found by code reading. No test covers it.

entries.name: ctx.blockConcurrencyWhile()
entries.cloudflare: Runs a callback while no other event reaches the object. A failure or a 30 second timeout resets the object.
entries.orange: Same, in the constructor and later. Nesting has no limit. A constructor-time block times out after 30 seconds.
entries.notes: The 30 second timeout applies to every call, as on workerd.

entries.name: ctx.id
entries.cloudflare: The object's DurableObjectId.
entries.orange: Same. It is rebuilt from the Rivet actor key and stays stable across sleep.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.storage
entries.cloudflare: The object's storage API, backed by SQLite for new_sqlite_classes.
entries.orange: Same. Rivet's per-actor SQLite database backs it. Unknown members throw DurableObjectStorage.<name> is not implemented.
entries.notes: See the durable-object-storage and sql entries for each method.

entries.name: ctx.waitUntil()
entries.cloudflare: Keeps the object alive until the promise settles.
entries.orange: Same. Orange passes the promise to Rivet's waitUntil, which keeps the actor awake.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.abort()
entries.cloudflare: Resets the object: uncommitted writes are discarded, the current event fails, and the next event gets a new instance. Alarms retry unless retryAlarm is false.
entries.orange: Same outcome. Orange rolls back the open turn, breaks the output gate, and restarts the whole Rivet actor from durable storage. retryAlarm is honored.
entries.notes: The reset is a full Rivet actor restart, which is heavier than workerd's in-isolate reset.
entries.unverified: What a reset does to open WebSocket connections on Orange is not tested.

entries.name: ctx.acceptWebSocket()
entries.cloudflare: Accepts a WebSocketPair server socket for hibernation, with optional tags.
entries.orange: Same. It rejects sockets already accepted with accept().
entries.notes: See limit-hibernatable-websockets and limit-websocket-tags for limits.

entries.name: ctx.getWebSockets()
entries.cloudflare: Returns accepted hibernatable sockets, optionally filtered by tag. It includes sockets restored after hibernation.
