entries.orange: Same. A socket stays listed during its webSocketClose. A socket the client closed while the instance was dropped is dropped after webSocketClose runs in the new instance.
entries.notes: A client's close code can be lost in the Rivet gateway: in the recorded lifecycle probe, a clean client close reached webSocketClose as 1001, not 1000.

entries.name: ctx.getTags()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the tags of an accepted socket.
entries.orange: Same. It returns a copy and throws for sockets that are not registered.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.setWebSocketAutoResponse()
entries.cloudflare: Sets one request and response pair. A matching text frame gets the response without waking the object.
entries.orange: Same matching and response. The actor's socket host answers a matching text frame without building an instance or restarting the idle timer, also while the instance is dropped.
entries.notes: The handler is not called for a matching frame, as on Cloudflare. Binary frames never match.

entries.name: ctx.getWebSocketAutoResponse()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the current auto-response pair, or null.
entries.orange: Same. It returns a new pair object each time.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.getWebSocketAutoResponseTimestamp()
entries.cloudflare: Returns when the socket last got an automatic response, or null.
entries.orange: Same. The timestamp survives hibernation.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.setHibernatableWebSocketEventTimeout()
entries.cloudflare: Sets the maximum run time of a webSocketMessage, webSocketClose, or webSocketError handler, up to 7 days.
entries.orange: Same limit and storage. A timeout makes Rivet sleep the object.
entries.notes: The timeout cannot stop synchronous JavaScript that blocks the Node event loop.

entries.name: ctx.getHibernatableWebSocketEventTimeout()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the event timeout, or null.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.exports in a Durable Object
entries.cloudflare: Loopback bindings to the Worker's exported entrypoints and classes.
entries.orange: Returns the Worker's ctx.exports, the same object as `import { exports } from "cloudflare:workers"`.
entries.notes: Durable Object classes appear as their namespaces.

entries.name: ctx.props in a Durable Object
entries.cloudflare: Props passed by the caller of a ctx.exports or service binding.
entries.orange: A facet whose class came from ctx.exports.<Name>({ props }) sees those props. Every other object sees {}, as in workerd.
entries.notes: A namespace in ctx.exports is not callable yet, so ctx.exports.<Name>({ props }) works only for a class without a namespace binding. tests/durable-object-facet-props.test.ts compares the facet cases with workerd 1.20260903.1.

entries.name: ctx.container
entries.cloudflare: Controls the container attached to the object.
entries.orange: Classes listed under wrangler containers get a Container that runs one sandbox per object on ORANGE_SANDBOX_PROVIDER. start(), exec(), monitor(), destroy(), signal(), and getTcpPort().fetch() work. Other classes throw NotSupportedError.
entries.notes: Only Cloudflare Sandbox images run; other images and start({ entrypoint }) throw. exec({ pty }), exec({ stdin }), interceptOutboundHttp(), interceptAllOutboundHttp(), interceptOutboundHttps(), snapshotContainer(), and inspect() throw. setInactivityTimeout() is a no-op. See docs/modules/sandbox.mdx.

entries.name: ctx.facets
entries.cloudflare: Starts and manages child objects (facets) that share the parent's storage.
entries.orange: ctx.facets.get(), abort(), delete(), and clone() work. Each facet is a child Rivet Actor with its own SQLite storage, hosted by one generic actor definition, so any exported class works without a binding or migration. A string id becomes the facet's ctx.id, as in workerd. clone() returns at once and copies one synchronous row snapshot of the source facet and its children in the background; later calls to the source and destination wait for the copy.
entries.notes: clone() matches workerd's facet cloning test, including restarts, and survives ctx.abort() and a crash during the copy. It copies a source inside storage.transaction() after the commit, where workerd copies the state before it, and its synchronous read blocks the runtime process (1.6 s for 100 MB). Facets nest to a depth of 4 and cannot set alarms. ctx.facets is still excluded from the generated type checks. See docs/modules/durable-objects.mdx.

entries.name: ctx.restore() (persistent stubs)
entries.cloudflare: With the allow_irrevocable_stub_storage flag, restores stubs stored in storage.
entries.orange: Reading it throws DurableObjectState.restore is not implemented.
entries.notes: persistent-stubs-test: 0 of 20 pass.

entries.name: ctx.configureReadReplication()
entries.cloudflare: Only with the experimental replica_routing flag, which Cloudflare does not deploy.
entries.orange: Reading it throws DurableObjectState.configureReadReplication is not implemented.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: alarm() handler
entries.cloudflare: storage.setAlarm() runs the class alarm() handler at the scheduled time, at least once.
entries.orange: Same. A Rivet durable schedule fires the handler. Only one alarm handler runs at a time per object.
entries.notes: The alarm row commits first, then Orange updates the Rivet schedule. Startup repairs a missing or stale schedule after a crash.

entries.name: alarm() alarmInfo argument
entries.cloudflare: The handler gets { scheduledTime, retryCount, isRetry }.
entries.orange: Same. isRetry is true when retryCount is above 0.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Alarm retries
entries.cloudflare: A handler that throws is retried with exponential backoff, up to 6 times.
entries.orange: Same. Retries start at 2 seconds, double each time, and add up to 25% jitter. A setAlarm() or deleteAlarm() during the handler replaces the retry.
entries.notes: Backoff matches workerd's local alarm scheduler.

entries.name: setAlarm() without an alarm() handler
entries.cloudflare: setAlarm() throws when the class has no alarm() handler. It is allowed during the constructor.
entries.orange: Same message: Your Durable Object class must have an alarm() handler in order to call setAlarm().
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: WebSocket hibernation
entries.cloudflare: An object with only hibernatable sockets is evicted from memory. Sockets stay open, and the next frame wakes a new instance.
entries.orange: Emulated inside a running Rivet Actor. After 10 seconds with no event, Orange drops the object's instance and keeps the actor and its accepted sockets open. The next message, close, or error on a socket builds a new instance, which gets the sockets with their tags, attachments, and auto-response timestamps before its constructor runs.
entries.notes: Rivet has paused its WebSocket hibernation, so the actor stays awake while an accepted socket is open, and it sleeps only after its last accepted socket closes and 10 more seconds pass with no event. A connected object keeps its actor, sockets, and their state in memory. An auto-response frame is answered without building an instance or restarting the idle timer. An unclaimed upgrade or an RPC result that a caller still holds keeps the instance running. The event timeout cannot stop synchronous JavaScript.

entries.name: ws.serializeAttachment()
entries.cloudflare: Stores a structured-clone value with the socket that survives hibernation.
entries.orange: Same. Values use the V8 serializer, have no size limit, and are stored in Rivet connection state.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ws.deserializeAttachment()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the value stored with the socket, also after hibernation.
entries.orange: Same. Reads the value from Rivet connection state.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: EventSource in a Durable Object
entries.cloudflare: new EventSource() works inside an object event.
entries.orange: Same. The constructor accepts a Durable Object event context as well as a Worker request.
entries.notes: Outside both, it throws NotSupportedError, as on workerd.
entries.unverified: The saved eventsource tests run in a Worker. No saved test creates an EventSource inside a Durable Object.

entries.name: locationHint option
entries.cloudflare: get(id, { locationHint }) asks Cloudflare to create the object near a region.
entries.orange: Accepted and validated. It has no effect because all objects run on the local host.
entries.notes: An unknown hint throws TypeError, as on Cloudflare.

entries.name: Jurisdictions
entries.cloudflare: Restricts where an object runs and stores data, for example eu or fedramp.
entries.orange: Validated and kept on ids and stubs. Data stays on the local host.
entries.notes: See do-namespace-jurisdiction.

entries.name: Critical SQLite errors reset the object
entries.cloudflare: SQLITE_FULL, SQLITE_IOERR, SQLITE_NOMEM, and SQLITE_INTERRUPT break the object. Later calls throw, and the next event gets a new instance.
entries.orange: Same codes and behavior.
entries.notes: SQLITE_CORRUPT is not on the critical list in workerd or Orange.

entries.name: Durability of acknowledged writes
entries.cloudflare: A write is durable before any output that follows it is visible.
entries.orange: Same through the output gate. Rivet's whenDurable() confirms each commit.
entries.notes: An earlier fault-injection run lost 0 of 23 acknowledged writes when the engine was killed.
entries.unverified: The fault-injection count was measured on an earlier RivetKit build, not the pinned 0.0.0-feat-sqlite-sync preview.

entries.name: KV-backed Durable Objects (new_classes)
entries.cloudflare: A new_classes migration creates a class with the key-value storage backend.
entries.orange: Accepted. Classes created with new_classes are stored in SQLite like new_sqlite_classes classes.
entries.notes: Orange is looser than Cloudflare here: ctx.storage.sql works in these classes, where Cloudflare throws because the key-value backend has no SQL.

entries.name: renamed_classes migration
entries.cloudflare: Renames a class and keeps its objects and data.
entries.orange: Config load fails with Unsupported Durable Object migration fields: renamed_classes.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: deleted_classes migration
entries.cloudflare: Deletes a class and all its objects.
entries.orange: Config load fails with Unsupported Durable Object migration fields: deleted_classes.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: transferred_classes migration
entries.cloudflare: Moves a class and its objects from another Worker.
entries.orange: Config load fails with Unsupported Durable Object migration fields: transferred_classes.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Wrangler 4.129's schema lists tag, new_classes, new_sqlite_classes, renamed_classes, and deleted_classes. Whether it passes transferred_classes through to Orange is not checked.

entries.name: storage.get(key)
entries.cloudflare: Returns the value for one key, or undefined.
entries.orange: Same. Values are stored in SQLite with the V8 serializer. A number key is converted to a string, as in workerd.
entries.notes: noCache is accepted and has no effect. allowConcurrency has no effect on SQLite storage, as on Cloudflare.

entries.name: storage.get(keys[])
entries.cloudflare: Returns a Map of found keys in key order. The KV backend takes at most 128 keys.
entries.orange: Same. Missing keys are left out and keys sort by UTF-8 bytes.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.put(key, value)
entries.cloudflare: Stores one structured-clone value.
entries.orange: Same. An undefined value throws put() called with undefined value.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.put(entries)
entries.cloudflare: Stores key-value pairs atomically. The KV backend takes at most 128 pairs.
entries.orange: Same. Fields whose value is undefined are skipped, as in workerd.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: put() allowUnconfirmed option
entries.cloudflare: Lets outgoing messages leave before the write is durable.
entries.orange: Same. The output gate does not wait for this write.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: put() noCache option
entries.cloudflare: Skips the in-memory storage cache for this write.
entries.orange: Validated and has no effect, because Orange has no storage cache.
entries.notes: Reads after a noCache write still go to storage, so results are the same. Only memory use differs.

entries.name: storage.delete(key)
entries.cloudflare: Deletes one key and returns whether it existed.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.delete(keys[])
entries.cloudflare: Deletes keys atomically and returns how many existed. The KV backend takes at most 128 keys.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.list()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a Map of all keys in key order.
entries.orange: Same. Writes earlier in the same turn are visible.
entries.notes: Orange reads the whole key table and filters in JavaScript, so a list on a large store costs more than on Cloudflare.

entries.name: list() start option
entries.cloudflare: Lists keys at or after start.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: start and startAfter together throw TypeError.

entries.name: list() startAfter option
entries.cloudflare: Lists keys after startAfter.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: list() end option
entries.cloudflare: Lists keys before end.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: An inverted range returns an empty Map.

entries.name: list() prefix option
entries.cloudflare: Lists keys that start with prefix.
entries.orange: Same, compared as UTF-8 bytes.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: list() reverse option
entries.cloudflare: Lists keys in descending order.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: list() limit option
entries.cloudflare: Returns at most limit entries. limit must be positive.
entries.orange: Same. A limit that is not a positive integer throws List limit must be positive.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.deleteAll()
entries.cloudflare: Deletes all keys, all SQL tables, and, from compatibility date 2026-02-24, the alarm.
entries.orange: Same. It drops every user table, view, virtual table, and trigger, keeps Rivet's private schema, and deletes the alarm. It throws inside a transaction. Open SQL cursors are canceled.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.transaction()
entries.cloudflare: Runs an async closure in a transaction. A throw or txn.rollback() rolls it back. Other events wait.
entries.orange: Same. The closure runs in a critical section of the input gate. Nested calls use savepoints. A handle used after commit throws.
entries.notes: See do-input-gate for the gap with events that are already running.

entries.name: storage.transactionSync()
entries.cloudflare: Runs a sync closure as a savepoint. A throw rolls it back.
entries.orange: Same. Nested calls use savepoints. An async transaction inside it is rejected.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.sync()
entries.cloudflare: Resolves when all earlier writes are durable.
entries.orange: Same. It commits the open turn and waits for Rivet to confirm durability.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.setAlarm()
entries.cloudflare: Schedules the alarm for a time. A past time runs it at once. A time <= 0 throws.
entries.orange: Same. Alarm writes join transactions and roll back with them.
entries.notes: See do-alarms for scheduling details.

entries.name: storage.getAlarm()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the scheduled time, or null. It is null while the alarm runs, unless the handler sets a new one.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.deleteAlarm()
entries.cloudflare: Cancels the scheduled alarm.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.storage.kv.get()
entries.cloudflare: Synchronous get of one key.
entries.orange: Same, on the same SQLite table as the async API.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.storage.kv.put()
entries.cloudflare: Synchronous put of one key.
entries.orange: Same. A value that cannot be cloned throws DataCloneError.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.storage.kv.delete()
entries.cloudflare: Synchronous delete of one key. Returns whether it existed.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: No saved upstream test calls kv.delete(). Orange's own sync-kv unit tests cover it.

entries.name: ctx.storage.kv.list()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a lazy iterator. A new list() call invalidates the previous iterator.
entries.orange: Same options and invalidation rule. The matching rows are read when list() is called, not while iterating.
entries.notes: Large lists use more memory. Writes made after list() do not show in the iterator.
entries.unverified: Whether workerd's iterator shows writes made after list() is not compared.

entries.name: storage.getCurrentBookmark()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a bookmark string for the current point in time.
entries.orange: Same format as workerd local development. Bookmarks increase on every call and persist in the _cf_METADATA table.
entries.notes: Bookmarks are not interchangeable with Cloudflare's.

entries.name: storage.getBookmarkForTime()
entries.cloudflare: Returns a bookmark for a past time, within the last 30 days.
entries.orange: Reading it throws DurableObjectStorage.getBookmarkForTime is not implemented.
entries.notes: Orange keeps no history, so point-in-time recovery is not possible.

entries.name: storage.onNextSessionRestoreBookmark()
entries.cloudflare: Restores the object's storage to a bookmark on the next restart.
entries.orange: Reading it throws DurableObjectStorage.onNextSessionRestoreBookmark is not implemented.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: storage.waitForBookmark()
entries.cloudflare: workerd exposes it only with the experimental flag. Cloudflare does not deploy it.
entries.orange: Present. It resolves at once because one local database is always up to date.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: ctx.storage.sql.exec()
entries.cloudflare: Runs one SQL statement with ? bindings and returns a cursor.
entries.orange: Same, through RivetKit SQLite 3.46.0. Errors end with the SQLite result code, for example no such table: x: SQLITE_ERROR.
entries.notes: The wrong number of bindings throws Wrong number of parameter bindings for SQL query. sql-test main fails with a RivetKit internal_error.
entries.unverified: The cause of the sql-test main failure (RivetKit internal_error) is not diagnosed.

entries.name: SQL binding value types
entries.cloudflare: Numbers, strings, null, and ArrayBuffer and views bind as themselves. Other values bind as their string form, so true binds "true". BigInt throws TypeError.
entries.orange: Same. Typed arrays and resizable ArrayBuffers bind as blobs.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: SQL result value types
entries.cloudflare: Results are number, string, null, or ArrayBuffer. A 64-bit integer outside the safe range is a lossy number, not a BigInt.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cursor.toArray()
entries.cloudflare: Returns all remaining rows as objects.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cursor.one()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the only row. Throws when there are 0 or more than 1 rows.
entries.orange: Same messages.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cursor.raw()
entries.cloudflare: Iterates rows as arrays. It shares the position with object iteration.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cursor.next()
entries.cloudflare: Returns the next row as an iterator result.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cursor[Symbol.iterator]()
entries.cloudflare: The cursor is an iterable of row objects.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: cursor.columnNames
entries.cloudflare: The result column names.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: For an empty multi-statement result, Orange returns no column names.

entries.name: cursor.rowsRead
entries.cloudflare: The rows SQLite read, including rows scanned. It grows while you iterate.
entries.orange: The number of rows returned.
entries.notes: Wrong for scans, index lookups, and aggregates. readRowCounters and largeRowCounters fail.
entries.workaround: Do not use rowsRead for cost estimates.

entries.name: cursor.rowsWritten
entries.cloudflare: The rows SQLite wrote, including index rows and trigger writes.
entries.orange: sqlite3_changes() for statements that start with INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or REPLACE. 0 otherwise.
entries.notes: Differs for triggers, upserts, index writes, and DDL. writeRowCounters and triggerRowCounters fail.

entries.name: Lazy SQL cursors
entries.cloudflare: exec() returns a live cursor that steps SQLite as you iterate.
entries.orange: exec() reads all rows at once. The cursor iterates the stored rows.
entries.notes: Large results use more memory. Counters are final at once. deleteAll() still cancels unread cursors.

entries.name: Multi-statement exec()
entries.cloudflare: Runs every statement. The cursor is for the last statement. Bindings apply to the last statement.
entries.orange: Runs every statement, but the cursor returns rows from every statement, with rowsWritten 0. Bindings throw OpenOrange does not yet support bindings on multi-statement SQL.
entries.notes: SELECT then UPDATE returns the SELECT rows on Orange and none on workerd.

entries.name: BEGIN, COMMIT, and SAVEPOINT in SQL
entries.cloudflare: exec() rejects transaction statements and points to transaction() and transactionSync().
entries.orange: Same message, also inside multi-statement SQL.
entries.notes: Statements before the rejected one still run, as on workerd.

entries.name: Reserved _cf_ table names
entries.cloudflare: SQL that names a _cf_ object fails, for example access to _cf_KV.key is prohibited.
entries.orange: A text check blocks _cf_ and _rivet_ names with not authorized.
entries.notes: Access is blocked, but the message differs, and _rivet_ names are also reserved. RivetKit's 16 internal _rivet_ tables and indexes always appear in sqlite_master and cannot be read.

entries.name: Authorizer in DEFAULT expressions
entries.cloudflare: The SQLite authorizer also checks functions in column DEFAULT expressions.
entries.orange: No authorizer runs. Blocked functions in DEFAULT expressions run.
entries.notes: Orange has no native SQLite authorizer.

entries.name: SQL function allow-list
entries.cloudflare: Only allowed SQL functions run. Internal functions are blocked outside a nested parse.
entries.orange: No allow-list. Internal functions run.
entries.notes: internalFunctionsBlocked fails with Missing expected exception.

entries.name: PRAGMA allow-list
entries.cloudflare: Only allow-listed PRAGMAs run, such as table_info, foreign_keys, and optimize. Others fail with not authorized.
entries.orange: Orange has no PRAGMA allow-list. RivetKit SQLite decides which PRAGMAs run.
entries.notes: A PRAGMA that Cloudflare rejects can run on Orange and change database settings.
entries.unverified: Found by code reading. regulatorReservedNames fails before its PRAGMA and ATTACH checks run, so no saved test covers them.

entries.name: DELETE and UPDATE with LIMIT
entries.cloudflare: DELETE ... LIMIT and UPDATE ... LIMIT work.
entries.orange: Fails with near "LIMIT": syntax error: SQLITE_ERROR. RivetKit's SQLite build lacks the grammar rule.
entries.notes: The compile flag alone does not help. The amalgamation must be generated with the flag.
entries.workaround: Use DELETE ... WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid ... LIMIT n).

entries.name: sql.databaseSize
entries.cloudflare: The database size in bytes.
entries.orange: Same formula as workerd: used pages times the page size.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: sql.ingest()
entries.cloudflare: workerd exposes it only with an experimental flag. Cloudflare does not deploy it.
entries.orange: Absent. Calling it throws TypeError.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: sql.prepare()
entries.cloudflare: workerd exposes it only with an experimental flag. Cloudflare does not deploy it.
entries.orange: Absent. Calling it throws TypeError.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: compatibility_date
entries.cloudflare: Selects runtime behavior by date. Each flag with an enable date turns on for Workers with that date or later.
entries.orange: Accepted with no warning, and nothing applies it. The runtime always behaves like workerd at 2026-09-03 with nodejs_compat. A missing date defaults to 2026-09-03.
entries.notes: The date only reaches the normalized configuration that feeds version metadata. A Worker with an older or newer date gets the 2026-09-03 behavior.

entries.name: compatibility_flags
entries.cloudflare: Turns individual runtime behaviors on or off, on top of the compatibility date.
entries.orange: Ignored. Config load prints `[config-warning] Orange ignores compatibility_flags ["..."]` with every distinct flag, sorted. The Node.js flags nodejs_compat, nodejs_compat_v2, and nodejs_als get `Orange always has Node.js APIs, so it does not need compatibility_flags ["..."]` instead.
entries.notes: The supported flag list is empty, so every flag gets a warning. The Worker still starts.

entries.name: Cloudflare.compatibilityFlags
entries.cloudflare: A frozen, prototype-less object that reports each enable flag as true or false for the running Worker.
entries.orange: A frozen, prototype-less table with fixed values for the 2026-09-03 profile with nodejs_compat. Configured flags do not change it, and the runtime does not read it.
entries.notes: Some values do not match runtime behavior. See the flag entries. compat-flags-test and compat-flag-enabled-test pass.

entries.name: nodejs_compat
entries.cloudflare: Enables Node.js built-in modules and globals. On by default for compatibility dates on or after 2026-08-04.
entries.orange: Always on. Built-in modules resolve whether or not the flag is set, and the table reports true.
entries.notes: Setting the flag prints the ignored-flag warning. no_nodejs_compat is also ignored, so built-ins still resolve.

entries.name: nodejs_compat_v2
entries.cloudflare: Implied by nodejs_compat on recent dates. Adds Node.js globals such as Buffer and process, and process.getBuiltinModule().
entries.orange: Always on, and the table reports true. node-compat-v2-test passes 4 of 5.
entries.notes: nodeJsGetBuiltins fails. A node:fs or node:path module in the Worker bundle does not override the built-in the way workerd does, or process.getBuiltinModule() returns a different module.
entries.unverified: Which half of nodeJsGetBuiltins fails is not checked.

entries.name: js_rpc
entries.cloudflare: Experimental and off. A Durable Object class that does not extend DurableObject rejects RPC.
entries.orange: Off, the same as Cloudflare. RPC to a plain class fails with `The receiving Durable Object does not support RPC, because its class was not declared with \`extends DurableObject\`...`.
entries.notes: Turning the flag on has no effect, so js-rpc-flag fails. Cloudflare does not deploy experimental flags.

entries.name: enable_request_signal
entries.cloudflare: Off by default. Without the flag, the incoming request.signal never aborts.
entries.orange: The table says false, but the incoming request.signal always aborts when the client disconnects or stops reading the response.
entries.notes: Code that works in Orange because request.signal aborts does not get the abort on Cloudflare unless the flag is set. request-signal-enabled passes 5 of 6. abortedRequestDoesNotAbortSubrequest fails.
entries.workaround: Set enable_request_signal in the Wrangler config so Cloudflare matches Orange.

entries.name: request_signal_passthrough
entries.cloudflare: Off by default. When on, a Request passed over RPC keeps its signal.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false. A Request passed over RPC has no signal, and setting the flag does not change that.
entries.notes: The default side passes requestPassedOverRpcDoesNotIncludeSignal. The opt-in side fails request-signal-passthrough.

entries.name: enable_nodejs_inspector_local_dev
entries.cloudflare: Experimental and local-dev only. Without it, the node:inspector Session constructor throws.
entries.orange: Stock Node.js node:inspector.
entries.notes: Session works as if the flag is on. Orange is looser than Cloudflare here: Node.js capabilities that workerd removes or stubs are available.

entries.name: nodejs_compat_populate_process_env
entries.cloudflare: Implied by nodejs_compat after 2025-04-01. Text and JSON bindings appear on process.env, and nothing else does.
entries.orange: On. Vars and secrets are copied to process.env, over the host environment of the runtime process.
entries.notes: Host variables such as RIVETKIT_STORAGE_PATH are visible. See process-env.

entries.name: durable_object_alarms
entries.cloudflare: Obsolete. Alarms are on for every Worker, and the flag reads false.
entries.orange: The table says false, and alarms work, the same as Cloudflare.
entries.notes: Not a mismatch.

entries.name: allow_eval_during_startup
entries.cloudflare: On by default since 2025-06-01. eval() and new Function() work while the Worker starts and throw `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` during a request.
entries.orange: The table says true, and eval() and new Function() work at all times, including during requests. Orange behaves as if the experimental allow_insecure_inefficient_logged_eval flag is on, while the table says false for it.
entries.notes: Code that calls eval() in a handler works in Orange and fails on Cloudflare. worker-test testStartupEval and new-module-registry-startup-eval-test fail. experimental-eval-test passes.

entries.name: spec_compliant_dispatch_exceptions
entries.cloudflare: On by default from 2026-09-15, so off at 2026-09-03. When off, an exception in an event listener propagates out of dispatchEvent().
entries.orange: The table says false, but listener exceptions do not propagate out of dispatchEvent(), as if the flag is on.
entries.notes: legacy-dispatch-exceptions-test, which sets no_spec_compliant_dispatch_exceptions, passes 1 of 4. Orange matches Cloudflare only for compatibility dates on or after 2026-09-15.
entries.unverified: No saved test checks the spec-compliant side, so full agreement with it is not verified.

entries.name: disallow_importable_env
entries.cloudflare: Off by default. When on, `env` and `exports` from cloudflare:workers are not populated.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false, and `import { env, exports } from "cloudflare:workers"` always returns the live objects. Setting the flag does not change that.
entries.notes: The default side works. Both disable-importable tests fail because the flag has no effect.

entries.name: new_module_registry
entries.cloudflare: Off by default. When on, workerd resolves unbundled modules at runtime by URL.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false. Orange always bundles the Worker with esbuild, and setting the flag only prints the ignored-flag warning.
entries.notes: Orange runs only the default side (flag off), which matches. The opt-in side is out of scope: upstream.json scores new-module-registry-test as not supported. Same status as the new_module_registry runtime entry.

entries.name: enable_web_file_system
entries.cloudflare: Experimental. Enables the Web File System API (navigator.storage, FileSystemFileHandle). Cloudflare does not deploy experimental flags.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false. navigator.storage and the FileSystem handle classes are missing.
entries.notes: webfs-test, webfs-ts-test, and ts-webfs-writable-test are scored as not supported.

entries.name: rtti_api
entries.cloudflare: Experimental. Enables the workerd:rtti module. Cloudflare does not deploy experimental flags.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false. Importing workerd:rtti prints a `[bundle-warning]` and throws `No such module "workerd:rtti"` when the importing module evaluates.
entries.notes: rtti-test fails at load.

entries.name: unsafe_module
entries.cloudflare: Experimental. Enables the workerd:unsafe module. Cloudflare does not deploy experimental flags.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false. Importing workerd:unsafe prints a `[bundle-warning]` and throws `No such module "workerd:unsafe"` when the importing module evaluates.
entries.notes: autogate-disabled-test is scored as test infrastructure because it imports workerd:unsafe.

entries.name: experimental
entries.cloudflare: Unlocks experimental flags in workerd. Cloudflare does not accept it for deployed Workers.
entries.orange: Off. The table says false. Setting it only prints the ignored-flag warning.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: precise_timers
entries.cloudflare: Experimental and off. Without it, Date.now() and performance.now() do not advance while code runs. They advance only after I/O.
entries.orange: The table says false, but Date.now() and performance.now() are Node.js clocks that advance during synchronous code, as if the flag is on.
entries.notes: Timing code that measures CPU work reads real elapsed time in Orange and zero on Cloudflare.
entries.unverified: No saved test checks clock advancement during synchronous code. The Cloudflare behavior is from the docs.

entries.name: $schema
entries.cloudflare: Points editors at the Wrangler JSON schema. Wrangler does not use it at runtime.
entries.orange: Ignored, the same as Wrangler.
entries.notes: Editor-only key.

entries.name: env
entries.cloudflare: Defines named environments that override top-level keys. `wrangler dev --env <name>` selects one.
entries.orange: `orange dev --env <name>` (or `-e`) passes the name to Wrangler's config reader, which applies the overrides.
entries.notes: Wrangler resolves inheritance, so non-inherited keys follow Wrangler's rules.

entries.name: name
entries.cloudflare: Names the Worker.
entries.orange: Used as the Worker name. A service binding or Durable Object binding that names this Worker is local. Any other name loads as a stub.
entries.notes: The name also feeds version metadata through the normalized configuration.

entries.name: account_id
entries.cloudflare: Selects the Cloudflare account for deploys and remote resources.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: main
entries.cloudflare: The Worker entrypoint module.
entries.orange: Bundled with esbuild and loaded as the Worker. Config load fails with `Wrangler configuration must resolve a Worker entrypoint` when Wrangler resolves no main.
entries.notes: A positional script argument to `orange dev` overrides main, the same as Wrangler. main is optional when assets is set, as in Wrangler.

entries.name: find_additional_modules
entries.cloudflare: Uploads files under base_dir that match rules as extra modules.
entries.orange: When true, config load fails with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: find_additional_modules.
entries.notes: Orange always bundles the Worker into one module.

entries.name: preserve_file_names
entries.cloudflare: Keeps original file names for additional modules on upload.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Only matters with find_additional_modules or rules, which Orange rejects.

entries.name: base_dir
entries.cloudflare: The directory where module rules are evaluated.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange does not pass it to esbuild.
entries.notes: Only matters with find_additional_modules or rules, which Orange rejects.

entries.name: workers_dev
entries.cloudflare: Publishes the Worker on its workers.dev subdomain.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: preview_urls
entries.cloudflare: Publishes preview URLs for each version.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: routes
entries.cloudflare: Routes traffic for zone patterns and custom domains to the Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange serves every request on its host and port.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: route
entries.cloudflare: A single route for the Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange serves every request on its host and port.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: tsconfig
entries.cloudflare: Wrangler passes this tsconfig path to esbuild.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange does not pass it to esbuild, so esbuild reads the nearest tsconfig.json to each file instead.
entries.notes: Settings from a tsconfig at a custom path, such as paths aliases or jsx options, do not apply.
entries.workaround: Name the file tsconfig.json next to the source files.

entries.name: jsx_factory
entries.cloudflare: Sets the JSX factory function for the Wrangler build. The default is React.createElement.
entries.orange: Ignored. esbuild uses its default or the value from tsconfig.json.
entries.notes: The default matches Wrangler. Only a non-default value differs.

entries.name: jsx_fragment
entries.cloudflare: Sets the JSX fragment function for the Wrangler build. The default is React.Fragment.
entries.orange: Ignored. esbuild uses its default or the value from tsconfig.json.
entries.notes: The default matches Wrangler. Only a non-default value differs.

entries.name: migrations
entries.cloudflare: An ordered list of Durable Object class migrations, each with a tag.
entries.orange: Accepted when every migration has only tag, new_sqlite_classes, and new_classes. Durable Object classes need an initial creation migration, or config load fails with `Durable Object classes require an initial new_sqlite_classes migration`.
entries.notes: renamed_classes, deleted_classes, and transferred_classes fail config load. Duplicate tags and a class created by more than one migration fail config load. See the sub-field entries.

entries.name: migrations[].new_sqlite_classes
entries.cloudflare: Creates SQLite-backed Durable Object classes.
entries.orange: Creates the classes. Every Durable Object binding class must appear in one new_sqlite_classes or new_classes list, or config load fails with `Durable Object class <name> is missing from new_sqlite_classes`.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: No saved test loads a config with a missing new_sqlite_classes entry. The synthetic suite only shows SQLite classes work.

entries.name: migrations[].renamed_classes
entries.cloudflare: Renames a Durable Object class and keeps its objects.
entries.orange: Config load fails with `Unsupported Durable Object migration fields: renamed_classes`.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: migrations[].deleted_classes
entries.cloudflare: Deletes a Durable Object class and its objects.
entries.orange: Config load fails with `Unsupported Durable Object migration fields: deleted_classes`.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: exports
entries.cloudflare: Declares Durable Object classes and entrypoints by class name, as an alternative to migrations.
entries.orange: A non-empty exports object fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: exports.
entries.notes: None.
entries.workaround: Declare Durable Object classes with migrations and new_sqlite_classes.

entries.name: triggers.crons
entries.cloudflare: Runs the scheduled handler on cron schedules.
entries.orange: Accepted. orange dev registers one Rivet cron job per expression in UTC and prints the next runs and a curl command for /cdn-cgi/local/scheduled.
entries.notes: Orange evaluates Cloudflare's cron syntax itself, including L, W, LW, #, and weekday 1 = Sunday. An expression that never matches or does not parse is skipped with a warning, where Cloudflare rejects it at deploy.

entries.name: triggers.events
entries.cloudflare: Runs the Worker on Cloudflare events, such as Artifacts events.
entries.orange: A non-empty list fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: triggers.events.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: limits.cpu_ms
entries.cloudflare: Sets the CPU time limit per invocation.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange enforces no CPU limit.
entries.notes: See limit-cpu-time.

entries.name: limits.subrequests
entries.cloudflare: Sets the subrequest limit per invocation.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange enforces no subrequest limit.
entries.notes: See subrequest-limits.

entries.name: rules
entries.cloudflare: Module rules that import Text, Data, and CompiledWasm modules by glob.
entries.orange: Applies the configured rules, then Wrangler's default rules, with Wrangler's fallthrough handling. Text imports load as strings, Data as ArrayBuffers, and CompiledWasm as WebAssembly.Module.
entries.notes: Globs match the import specifier, as in Wrangler. ESModule and CommonJS rules are skipped because Orange bundles. Python rule types fail config load.

entries.name: build.command
entries.cloudflare: Runs a custom build command before Wrangler bundles the Worker.
entries.orange: Runs the command through the shell in build.cwd before bundling. A non-zero exit stops orange dev with Running custom build `<command>` failed with exit code <code>.
entries.notes: There is no watch mode, so the command runs once per orange dev start.

entries.name: build.cwd
entries.cloudflare: The directory for build.command.
entries.orange: The directory build.command runs in, relative to the config file. Defaults to the config directory.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: build.watch_dir
entries.cloudflare: Directories that `wrangler dev` watches to rebuild.
entries.orange: Ignored. `orange dev` does not watch files or rebuild.
entries.notes: Restart `orange dev` after a change.

entries.name: no_bundle
entries.cloudflare: Skips bundling and uploads the modules as written.
entries.orange: Accepted. Orange still bundles the entry with esbuild, following the relative imports between the built modules.
entries.notes: Output from @cloudflare/vite-plugin, which sets no_bundle, runs. A module reached only through a computed import() path is not found.

entries.name: minify
entries.cloudflare: Minifies the bundle.
entries.orange: Ignored. The bundle is never minified.
entries.notes: Runtime behavior is the same except for function names and stack traces.

entries.name: keep_names
entries.cloudflare: Keeps function and class names during minification. The default is true.
entries.orange: Ignored. The bundle is not minified, so names are always kept.
entries.notes: The default matches. keep_names: false has no effect.

entries.name: first_party_worker
entries.cloudflare: Marks an internal Cloudflare first-party Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: logpush
entries.cloudflare: Sends trace events to Workers Logpush.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: upload_source_maps
entries.cloudflare: Uploads source maps with the Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored. The local bundle always has an inline source map.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: placement
entries.cloudflare: Smart Placement runs the Worker near its back ends.
entries.orange: Ignored. The Worker runs in the local process.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: assets
entries.cloudflare: Serves static assets, optionally through an ASSETS binding.
entries.orange: orange dev serves the assets directory with Wrangler's router and asset Worker rules: html_handling, not_found_handling, run_worker_first patterns, .assetsignore, and assets-only Workers.
entries.notes: _headers and _redirects are not applied, and orange dev warns when they exist. The 25 MiB file and 100,000 file limits are not enforced. The directory is read on every request.

entries.name: legacy_assets
entries.cloudflare: The legacy static assets key.
entries.orange: Any value fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: legacy_assets.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: site
entries.cloudflare: Workers Sites static assets.
entries.orange: Any value fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: site.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: pages_build_output_dir
entries.cloudflare: Marks a Pages project and its output directory.
entries.orange: Any value fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: pages_build_output_dir.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: observability
entries.cloudflare: Enables Workers Logs and traces with sampling.
entries.orange: Ignored. Console output goes to the `orange dev` terminal.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: access
entries.cloudflare: Configures Cloudflare Access authentication for the Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored. Requests reach the Worker without Access.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.
entries.unverified: Whether access.dev changes `wrangler dev` behavior is not checked.

entries.name: cache
entries.cloudflare: Enables the Workers cache in front of the Worker and its cross-version behavior.
entries.orange: Ignored. No cache runs in front of the Worker.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: The exact Cloudflare semantics of the cache key are from the schema description only.

entries.name: compliance_region
entries.cloudflare: Selects a compliance region for the deployed Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: python_modules
entries.cloudflare: Configures modules for Python Workers.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange does not run Python Workers.
entries.notes: A Python main cannot be bundled.
entries.unverified: The failure mode for a Python main is not run.

entries.name: previews
entries.cloudflare: Settings for preview deployments made with `wrangler preview`.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: define
entries.cloudflare: Replaces global identifiers with constant values at build time.
entries.orange: A non-empty define fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: define.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: secrets.required
entries.cloudflare: Lists the secrets the Worker needs. `wrangler dev` loads only these keys from .dev.vars or .env and warns about missing ones.
entries.orange: Passed to Wrangler's dev-vars loader. A missing secret prints `[config-warning] Missing required secrets: <names>. Add them to .dev.vars, .env, or set as environment variables.`
entries.notes: The Worker still starts without the secret.
entries.unverified: Whether Wrangler's loader filters .dev.vars keys to secrets.required is Wrangler behavior and is not run here.

entries.name: queues.consumers
entries.cloudflare: Runs the queue handler for messages on a queue.
entries.orange: Accepted. Each consumer starts the delivery loop of its queue actor with max_batch_size, max_batch_timeout, max_retries, retry_delay, and dead_letter_queue. Unset settings take Cloudflare's production defaults: 10, 5 s, 3, and 0.
entries.notes: A value outside Cloudflare's range stops orange dev and names the queue. max_concurrency is ignored. See docs/modules/queues.mdx.

entries.name: cloudchamber
entries.cloudflare: Configures Cloudchamber container deployments.
entries.orange: A non-empty object fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: cloudchamber.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: containers
entries.cloudflare: Configures Containers bound to Durable Object classes.
entries.orange: Accepted with one warning. No container image runs. Sandbox classes from @cloudflare/sandbox, and other classes listed under containers, run on the ORANGE_SANDBOX_PROVIDER backend (default: local).
entries.notes: A listed class's ctx.container runs one sandbox per object, and start() takes only a Cloudflare Sandbox image: an image reference or Dockerfile that names cloudflare/sandbox. A class that containers does not list throws NotSupportedError from ctx.container. See do-ctx-container and docs/modules/sandbox.mdx.

entries.name: @cloudflare/sandbox (Sandbox SDK)
entries.cloudflare: Runs each Sandbox Durable Object in a Container with exec, processes, files, git, sessions, code interpreter, and preview URLs.
entries.orange: Orange replaces the package at bundle time. Each Sandbox Durable Object owns one sandbox on the ORANGE_SANDBOX_PROVIDER backend: local (default, not isolated), e2b, daytona, or freestyle. The sandbox id persists in the object storage and reconnects after restarts.
entries.notes: createSession, createCodeContext, and runCode throw. Preview URLs work with the local provider only. Background processes stop with orange dev. E2B, Daytona, and Freestyle are untested without API keys.

entries.name: connect
entries.cloudflare: Opens raw listening sockets that deliver connections to the Worker's connect handler.
entries.orange: A non-empty list fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: connect.
entries.notes: A connect handler on an entrypoint still works over service bindings and ctx.exports.

entries.name: tail_consumers
entries.cloudflare: Sends trace events to Tail Workers.
entries.orange: Accepted. After each traced event, the Worker appends its TraceItem to a Rivet Durable Streams stream of each consumer, and an openorange:tail actor in the consumer Worker reads the stream and calls tail(). A consumer can be the Worker itself or another Worker of the orange dev session.
entries.notes: Delivery is at least once: the stream offset moves only after tail() returns. orange dev starts one Rivet Services process for the session. On a cluster, the namespace needs a Services deployment in the envoy pool services. handler-tail lists which events are traced. See docs/modules/tail-workers.mdx.

entries.name: streaming_tail_consumers
entries.cloudflare: Sends streaming trace events to Tail Workers.
entries.orange: A non-empty list fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: streaming_tail_consumers.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: send_metrics
entries.cloudflare: Controls Wrangler usage metrics.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange sends no usage metrics.
entries.notes: Tool-only key.

entries.name: dependencies_instrumentation
entries.cloudflare: Controls npm dependency metadata sent on deploy.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: dev.ip
entries.cloudflare: The address `wrangler dev` listens on.
entries.orange: Ignored. `orange dev` listens on 127.0.0.1 unless --ip or --host is set.
entries.notes: The CLI flag works.

entries.name: dev.port
entries.cloudflare: The port `wrangler dev` listens on.
entries.orange: Ignored. `orange dev` listens on 8787 unless --port is set.
entries.notes: The CLI flag works.

entries.name: dev.local_protocol
entries.cloudflare: Serves `wrangler dev` over http or https.
entries.orange: Ignored. `orange dev` serves HTTP only. `--local-protocol https` fails with `OpenOrange dev currently supports only HTTP`.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: dev.upstream_protocol
entries.cloudflare: Sets the protocol of request.url in `wrangler dev`.
entries.orange: Ignored. request.url always uses http and the incoming Host header.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: dev.host
entries.cloudflare: Rewrites the host of request.url in `wrangler dev`.
entries.orange: Ignored. request.url uses the incoming Host header.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: dev.inspector_port
entries.cloudflare: The port of the `wrangler dev` DevTools inspector.
entries.orange: Ignored. `orange dev` opens no inspector port.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Whether the runtime child process can be inspected another way is not checked.

entries.name: alias
entries.cloudflare: Maps module specifiers to other modules at build time.
entries.orange: Ignored. Orange does not pass aliases to esbuild. An aliased import that does not resolve prints a `[bundle-warning]` and throws when the importing module evaluates.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: keep_vars
entries.cloudflare: Keeps dashboard vars on deploy.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-only key.

entries.name: addresses
entries.cloudflare: Creates Email Routing rules that send mail for these addresses to the Worker.
entries.orange: Ignored.
entries.notes: Deploy-time routing. The email handler loads and never runs.

entries.name: unsafe (non-binding fields)
entries.cloudflare: unsafe.metadata and unsafe.capnp change the upload metadata or the workerd config directly.
entries.orange: Any unsafe field other than bindings fails config load with Unsupported Wrangler configuration: unsafe.
entries.notes: unsafe.bindings is accepted. See the binding entries.

entries.name: Durable Object class without a binding
entries.cloudflare: A migrated class without a namespace binding is reachable through ctx.exports.
entries.orange: Same. A class in new_sqlite_classes needs no durable_objects binding.
entries.notes: When durable_objects is set, it needs a bindings array, which can be empty.

entries.name: Storage key size
entries.cloudflare: Key and value combined cannot exceed 2 MB.
entries.orange: No Cloudflare limit. Rivet's applies: one write stores at most 134,217,728 bytes (128 MiB) of changed SQLite pages, so a key of 128 MiB or more throws a RangeError that names that limit.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's 2 MB quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: Storage value size
entries.cloudflare: Key and value combined cannot exceed 2 MB.
entries.orange: No Cloudflare limit. Rivet's applies: a key and value of 128 MiB or more together throw a RangeError that names Rivet's 128 MiB commit limit. An 8 MiB value works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's 2 MB quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: Keys per multi-key put()
entries.cloudflare: No limit for SQLite-backed classes. At most 128 pairs for KV-backed classes.
entries.orange: No limit for any class.
entries.notes: workerd checks the 128 limit only in its KV backend (actor-cache.c++), not in its SQLite backend. Orange stores new_classes in SQLite too, so it is looser for KV-backed classes.

entries.name: Keys per multi-key get()
entries.cloudflare: No limit for SQLite-backed classes. At most 128 keys for KV-backed classes.
entries.orange: No limit for any class.
entries.notes: workerd checks the 128 limit only in its KV backend (actor-cache.c++), not in its SQLite backend. Orange stores new_classes in SQLite too, so it is looser for KV-backed classes.

entries.name: Keys per multi-key delete()
entries.cloudflare: No limit for SQLite-backed classes. At most 128 keys for KV-backed classes.
entries.orange: No limit for any class.
entries.notes: workerd checks the 128 limit only in its KV backend (actor-cache.c++), not in its SQLite backend. Orange stores new_classes in SQLite too, so it is looser for KV-backed classes.

entries.name: SQL statement length
entries.cloudflare: At most 100 KB per statement (SQLITE_LIMIT_SQL_LENGTH 100000).
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: Longer statements run on Orange and fail on Cloudflare.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: SQL bound parameters per query
entries.cloudflare: At most 100 bound parameters per query.
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: Queries with more than 100 parameters run on Orange and fail on Cloudflare.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: SQL columns per table
entries.cloudflare: At most 100 columns per table.
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: SQL string or BLOB size
entries.cloudflare: Each string or BLOB value is at most 2 MB.
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: SQL row size
entries.cloudflare: Each row is at most 2 MB.
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: LIKE and GLOB pattern length
entries.cloudflare: At most 50 bytes per LIKE or GLOB pattern.
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: Arguments per SQL function
entries.cloudflare: The documented limit is 32. workerd sets 127.
entries.orange: No Orange check. SQLite's build limit applies.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search. The limits in the pinned RivetKit SQLite build are not checked.

entries.name: Storage per Durable Object
entries.cloudflare: 10 GB per object on Workers Paid. Writes past it fail.
entries.orange: No limit. The object grows until the host disk is full.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Absence found by code search.

entries.name: Hibernatable WebSockets per object
entries.cloudflare: At most 32,768 accepted WebSockets per object.
entries.orange: No limit. Accepted sockets are bounded by memory.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: Tags per WebSocket
entries.cloudflare: At most 10 tags per hibernatable WebSocket.
entries.orange: No limit. A socket with 20 tags works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: WebSocket tag length
entries.cloudflare: Each tag is at most 256 bytes.
entries.orange: No limit. Tags of 300 bytes work.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: WebSocket attachment size
entries.cloudflare: serializeAttachment() accepts at most 16 KiB of serialized data.
entries.orange: No limit. A 64 KiB attachment works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: Hibernatable WebSocket event timeout
entries.cloudflare: setHibernatableWebSocketEventTimeout() accepts at most 604,800,000 ms (7 days).
entries.orange: Up to 2,147,483,647 ms (about 24.8 days), the longest delay of a Node.js timer, which runs the timeout. A 20-day timeout works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's 7-day quota is not copied. The bound is Node's.

entries.name: Auto-response request length
entries.cloudflare: The auto-response request string is at most 2,048 bytes.
entries.orange: No limit. A 4 KiB request works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: Auto-response response length
entries.cloudflare: The auto-response response string is at most 2,048 bytes.
entries.orange: No limit. A 4 KiB response works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's quota is not copied by design.

entries.name: Durable Object WebSocket message size
entries.cloudflare: Received WebSocket messages are at most 32 MiB.
entries.orange: No Orange check. Rivet's WebSocket transport limit applies.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Rivet's WebSocket message size limit is not checked.

entries.name: RPC payload size
entries.cloudflare: RPC values are at most 32 MiB.
entries.orange: No Cloudflare limit. Rivet's applies: a Durable Object RPC call is one message to the Rivet Engine, which takes at most 32 MiB, with binary data in base64. A larger call throws a RangeError that names that limit. A 16 MiB value works.
entries.notes: Cloudflare's 32 MiB quota is not copied. Measured: 23.9 MiB of bytes works and 24 MiB is over the Engine's limit after base64.

entries.name: Alarm retries
entries.cloudflare: A failing alarm handler retries up to 6 times.
entries.orange: Same.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: Backoff timing is compared with workerd only, not with Cloudflare production.

entries.name: blockConcurrencyWhile() nesting depth
entries.cloudflare: Nesting deeper than 64 throws.
entries.orange: No limit. Nesting 200 deep works.
entries.notes: Workerd's limit protects its native stack. Orange nests in JavaScript.

entries.name: CPU time per invocation
entries.cloudflare: 10 ms on Free. 30 s by default on Paid, configurable up to 5 minutes with limits.cpu_ms. Over the limit, the invocation fails.
entries.orange: Not enforced.
entries.notes: A handler can run as long as it needs. Code that passes in Orange can exceed the Cloudflare limit.

entries.name: Memory per isolate
entries.cloudflare: 128 MB per isolate. Over the limit, the isolate is reset.
entries.orange: Not enforced.
entries.notes: The runtime process uses the Node.js heap default.

entries.name: Subrequests per invocation
entries.cloudflare: 50 on Free and a higher configurable limit on Paid. Over the limit, fetch() throws.
entries.orange: Not enforced.
entries.notes: fetch() and binding calls are never counted.
entries.unverified: The current Paid default is from the docs page and is not restated here.

entries.name: Simultaneous open connections
entries.cloudflare: 6 per invocation. Extra fetch() calls and sockets wait for a free connection.
entries.orange: Not enforced.
entries.notes: Orange opens as many connections in parallel as the code starts.

entries.name: Request body size
entries.cloudflare: 100 MB on Free and Pro, 200 MB on Business, 500 MB on Enterprise. Larger requests get 413.
entries.orange: Not enforced. The body streams into the Worker without a size check.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Response body size
entries.cloudflare: No limit on a streamed response body.
entries.orange: No limit. The response streams to the client.
entries.notes: Cache limits do not apply because Orange has no cache.

entries.name: URL length
entries.cloudflare: 16 KB. Longer URLs get 414.
entries.orange: Not enforced by Orange. Node.js counts the request line toward its header size limit.
entries.notes: See limit-request-headers.
entries.unverified: The exact Node.js behavior for a long URL is not run.

entries.name: Request header size
entries.cloudflare: 128 KB of request headers.
entries.orange: Uses the Node.js HTTP server default of 16 KiB for the request line and headers. Larger requests get 431.
entries.notes: Orange is stricter than Cloudflare. Requests with 16 KiB to 128 KB of headers work on Cloudflare and fail in Orange.
entries.unverified: The 16 KiB threshold is the Node.js default and is not run against Orange.

entries.name: Environment variable count
entries.cloudflare: At most 64 variables on Free and 128 on Paid.
entries.orange: Not enforced. Any number of vars load.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Environment variable size
entries.cloudflare: Each variable is at most 5 KB.
entries.orange: Not enforced. Vars of any size load.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Worker size
entries.cloudflare: 3 MB on Free and 10 MB on Paid, after compression. Larger Workers fail to deploy.
entries.orange: Not enforced. Any bundle size loads.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Worker startup time
entries.cloudflare: 1 s to parse and run the global scope. Over the limit, deploy fails.
entries.orange: Not enforced. The global scope can run as long as it needs.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Workers per account
entries.cloudflare: 100 on Free and 500 on Paid.
entries.orange: Orange runs one Worker per process.
entries.notes: None.

entries.name: Cron triggers per account
entries.cloudflare: 5 on Free and 250 on Paid.
entries.orange: orange dev runs every configured cron. It has no per-account limit.
entries.notes: See config-cron-triggers.

entries.name: Console log size
entries.cloudflare: Workers Logs truncates large log lines and caps log volume per invocation.
entries.orange: Not enforced. console output goes to the `orange dev` terminal in full.
entries.notes: None.
entries.unverified: The exact Cloudflare log size caps are not restated.
